The AGC has four step gains that are inversely proportional to the amplitude of their input signal. Accordingly, the AGC reduces the dynamic range of the signal entering the CFD and consequently reduces the dependency of the response time on the input signal, i.e., time walk. For a short resolving time, this gain setting is performed at one time by amplitude comparison. The proposed CFD is evaluated by experiment for input signals with a rise time of 2 ns and a dynamic range of 40 dB, and the time walk is reduced to 277 ps, a decrease of more than 42%.

title: Closed-Form Design of Half-Sample Delay IIR Filter Using Continued Fraction Expansion
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I: Regular Papers
abstract: In this paper, the closed-form design of half-sample delay infinite-impulse response (IIR) filter is presented. First, the continued fraction expansion (CFE) and its recursive computation are reviewed briefly. Then, the CFE of square root function is applied to design half-sample delay IIR filters with various orders. The comparisons with conventional maximally flat half-sample delay all-pass and Lagrange filters are made and implementation issue is also addressed. Next, the designed half-sample delay filter is used to reduce the approximation error of the conventional IIR Simpson integrator, to design half-band and diamond shaped filters, and to magnify the digital image. Finally, several numerical examples are illustrated to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed design method

title: Observer-Based Active Disturbance Rejection Control for Fraction-Delay Grid-Tied Inverters
authors: Dingcheng Zhang; Qiang Qian; Zhuolin Yang; Li Zhang; Jinming Xu
venue: 2025 IEEE 16th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Aiming at damping high-frequency resonances, the pulse-width modulation strategy characterized by reduced control delay is gaining attention in grid-tied inverter. However, the outcome of the fractional ratio of the sampling-computation period to the control period challenges the discrete-time state-space modeling and the control implementation. Therefore, a delay-based input matrix is proposed for discretizing the fraction-delay system, which further facilitates the application of active disturbance rejection control. The observer is also exemplified by introducing a feedback of the error of the observable state, which avoids using extra sensors. Finally, experiments are conducted on a grid-tied inverter to corroborate the effectiveness of the model and the modern control method.

title: Design and analysis of a jitter-tolerant digital delay-locked-loop based fraction-of-clock delay line
authors: J.R. Burnham; G.K. Yeh; E. Sun; Chih-Kong Ken Yang
venue: 2004 IEEE International Solid-State Circuits Conference (IEEE Cat. No.04CH37519)
abstract: A digital DLL-based fraction-of-clock delay line is described. It uses a combination of scaling and phase-detector window alignment to improve jitter tolerance and loop stability without requiring a loop filter or reducing tracking bandwidth.

title: Reducing energy costs in Internet-scale distributed systems using load shifting
authors: Vimal Mathew; Ramesh K. Sitaraman; Prashant Shenoy
venue: 2014 Sixth International Conference on Communication Systems and Networks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Energy costs have become a significant fraction of the operational costs of running large Internet-scale distributed systems (IDS). In this work, we propose a demand-response technique where the system temporarily reduces its energy usage in response to pricing signals from a smart grid. Our proposed demand-response technique involves deferring the load from elastic requests to later time periods in order to reduce the server demand and the current energy usage, and hence, energy costs. We propose an optimal offline algorithm for demand response and evaluate it on production workloads from a commercial content delivery network using realistic electricity pricing models. Our optimal offline algorithm can achieve 12% energy cost savings for time-of-use electricity pricing, even when only 40% of the load is elastic and the service delay is at most 6 hours. The savings increase to 32% under peak-based demand pricing and to 23% under a combination of time-of-use and demand pricing. Further, we show that almost all the energy cost savings can be achieved with no increase in the bandwidth cost of the IDS.

title: Cascade-parallel realization of 2-D separable-denominator transfer functions using a variant partial-fraction expansion
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A direct procedure based on using a variant partial-fraction expansion (VPFE) is presented for finding a canonical minimal realization of cascade-parallel structure for 2-D transfer functions having a separable denominator. A similarity transforming matrix that transforms a 2-D separable-denominator state-space model from a phase-variable canonical form to the VPFE canonical form is presented. A numerical example is provided to illustrate the procedure.<>

title: Stability and Stabilization of Delayed T--S Fuzzy Systems: A Delay Partitioning Approach
authors: Yan Zhao; Huijun Gao; James Lam; Baozhu Du
abstract: This paper proposes a new approach, namely, the delay partitioning approach, to solving the problems of stability analysis and stabilization for continuous time-delay Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy systems. Based on the idea of delay fractioning, a new method is proposed for the delay-dependent stability analysis of fuzzy time-delay systems. Due to the instrumental idea of delay partitioning, the proposed stability condition is much less conservative than most of the existing results. The conservatism reduction becomes more obvious with the partitioning getting thinner. Based on this, the problem of stabilization via the so-called parallel distributed compensation scheme is also solved. Both the stability and stabilization results are further extended to time-delay fuzzy systems with time-varying parameter uncertainties. All the results are formulated in the form of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), which can be readily solved via standard numerical software. The advantage of the results proposed in this paper lies in their reduced conservatism, as shown via detailed illustrative examples. The idea of delay partitioning is well demonstrated to be efficient for conservatism reduction and could be extended to solving other problems related to fuzzy delay systems.

title: Reduced-Order Transfer Function Model of the Droop-Controlled Inverter via Jordan Continued-Fraction Expansion
authors: Wang Rui; Sun Qiuye; Zhang Pinjia; Gui Yonghao; Qin Dehao; Wang Peng
abstract: This article proposes a reduced-order small-signal closed-loop transfer function model based on Jordan continued-fraction expansion to assess the dynamic characteristics of the droop-controlled inverter and provide the preprocessing method for the real-time simulation of power systems. Firstly, dynamic phasors, time delay and zero-order hold are embedded into the small-signal model at the same time, then the closed-loop transfer function of the droop-controlled inverter is built. Compared with the existing closed-loop transfer function approaches, the accuracy of the built transfer function model is dramatically enhanced. Meanwhile, the inner cascaded voltage/current controller parameters are also designed. In order to directly obtain and preserve the maximum overshoot and settling time, which are main features to evaluate the system input-output dynamic response characteristics, the reduced second order closed-loop transfer function is proposed through the continued-fraction expansion regarding arbitrary points on the real frequency axis. Therein, this second order closed-loop transfer function with dynamic response of the original inverter is reduced to the lowest order. Furthermore, combined with the impedance-based approach, the proposed stability assessment approach is utilized to analyze the stability of the microgrid with multiple converters. Finally, simulations and experimental results demonstrate the convenience and accuracy of the proposed approach.

title: Modeling Research on Tropospheric Delay Mapping Function
authors: Ruoyu Li; Leke Lin; Xiangming Chen; Qiang Zhang
venue: 2023 Cross Strait Radio Science and Wireless Technology Conference (CSRSWTC)
abstract: Due to the increasing demands for atmospheric refraction in radio systems, the investigation of atmospheric propagation errors has emerged as a primary approach to enhancing system accuracy. The mapping function plays a crucial role in accurately converting zenith direction delay to the signal transmission path direction, thus serving as a vital parameter for analyzing tropospheric delays. To enhance the accuracy of slant path delay in radio systems, this study utilizes meteorological sounding data from the Qingdao station in 2022, including pressure, temperature, humidity, and other variables. By employing the parameter fitting method, a rational mapping function model is established. The results demonstrate that the new mapping function model outperforms traditional models in calculating slant path delays, particularly in reducing error in the wet term delay. This improvement carries significant implications for enhancing the accuracy of radio systems.

title: E-commerce Supply Chain Cost Optimization with Incentive Compatibility Constraints
authors: Sahani Rathnasiri; Pritee Ray; Sardar M.N. Islam; Carlos A. Vega-Mejía
venue: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: Even though the e-commerce supply chain operations have paid continuous attention in improving their operational capabilities and optimizing costs, strategic interactions and management issues still exist, thereby impeding the optimal performances. Game theory-based contract models have vastly been adopted in supply chain studies to resolve issues of strategic interactions and decision-making among different supply chain members. In that context, contracts include incentive compatibility constraints to ensure that the players have sufficient incentive to remain within the contract. However, less attention has been given to contract models, which includes multi-levels of e-commerce-based supply chain operations. Therefore, this study develops a cost-sharing contract, including incentive compatibility constraints for the three-level e-commerce supply chain to address the issues of cost information asymmetry. We consider cost information asymmetry issues of the upstream and downstream of the supply chain where e-tailer shares a fraction of operational costs of the product supplier and the 3PL operator. The results of this study emphasize that the cost-sharing contract significantly reduces the overall supply chain cost while proving Pareto-improved outcomes in terms of cost minimization.

title: Modeling and analysis of crosstalk coupling effect on the victim interconnect using the ABCD network model
authors: A.K. Palit; V. Meyer; W. Anheier; J. Schloeffel
venue: 19th IEEE International Symposium on Defect and Fault Tolerance in VLSI Systems, 2004. DFT 2004. Proceedings.
abstract: After order reduction, the crosstalk model is utilized for the analysis of crosstalk coupling effects on the victim's output signal. Various timing issues related to signal waveform such as, delay time, overshoot and undershoot occurrence time etc., that in effect help to ensure the desired signal integrity (SI) and performance reliability of the SoCs, can be estimated analytically using the reduced order crosstalk model. It has been observed that the crosstalk coupling effect introduces a delay in the victim's output signal which can be significant enough, or even unacceptable, if many aggressors simultaneously couple energy to the victim line, or the line spacing between the aggressor and victim is reduced due to under-etching ,or even, the length of the victim interconnect is increased because of improper layout/routing. Influences of other interconnect parasitics on the victim's output signal can also be tested using the same model. Simulation results obtained with our reduced order model is found to be quite good and comparable to the accuracy of PSPICE simulation.

title: A Loop Delay Estimation Algorithm Based on Sliding Window in Digital Predistortion Systems
authors: Jing Zhang; Weimin Li; Haoyang Duan; Menghao Wang
venue: 2023 3rd International Symposium on Computer Technology and Information Science (ISCTIS)
abstract: With the development of communication technology, the linearity of power amplifiers has become an important indicator of the modern communication systems, and digital predistortion (DPD) techniques have emerged in this context. When there is a delay between the output signal and the input signal, the performance of a DPD system is significantly reduced. To address the shortcomings of the widely used loop delay estimation algorithms, an integer loop delay algorithm based on sliding window and a fractional loop delay algorithm using cubic spline interpolation are proposed. The simulation results show that the algorithms not only have low complexity and good accuracy, but also exclude the problems of signal fading and noise interference, which makes them widely applicable to DPD systems.

title: Scheduling Policies for Wireless Downlink With Correlated Random Connectivity and Multislot Reconfiguration Delay
abstract: Stable and minimum delay scheduling of wireless downlinks, with time correlated random connectivity between the base station and each associated user, is an important problem in modern communication systems. We assume that the base station of the wireless downlink dynamically switches between the users to transmit packets to each user. The dynamic switching of the base station incurs a reconfiguration delay. We find that as the reconfiguration delay increases the stability region of the wireless downlink with correlated channel connectivity shrinks to that achieved by time sharing among the users over large time periods. Since existing scheduling policies are designed either for single slot reconfiguration delay and correlated random connectivity, or multislot reconfiguration delay but without correlated connectivity, we propose scheduling policies which explicitly takes into account the correlated channel connectivity and multislot reconfiguration delay and show using simulations that the average delay is reduced compared to existing policies.

title: Low-Cost Agricultural Robotics: An AI-Enabled Autonomous Rover
venue: 2025 IEEE 31st International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The prohibitive initial costs and operational complexities of commercial agricultural robots significantly impede the widespread adoption of precision agriculture, particularly for small and medium-sized farms, limiting crucial applications like early disease detection. This abstract presents a novel, low-cost, AI-enabled autonomous agricultural rover designed to overcome these barriers. By leveraging readily available and affordable components, this approach offers a cost-effective and easily adaptable platform, significantly reducing the financial entry point and simplifying maintenance compared to traditional commercial solutions. The prototype rover is engineered to perform critical field monitoring tasks, with a particular focus on early disease detection in young plant cultures. Utilizing integrated AI capabilities, the rover is designed for autonomous navigation and employs vision-based systems for real-time plant health assessment, identifying anomalies indicative of disease onset. This system demonstrates the feasibility of deploying advanced robotic solutions for targeted agricultural applications at a fraction of traditional costs. This work contributes to making precision agriculture technology more accessible to a wider range of farmers, fostering sustainable practices by enabling timely, localized interventions and enhancing crop resilience through proactive management.

title: Low cost floating-point unit design for audio applications
venue: 2002 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: This paper presents a low-cost single-cycle floating-point unit developed for digital audio processing applications. In the unit, the serial steps of floating-point operations are paralleled to reduce critical path delay, and hardware resources are shared with the integer datapath to minimize area overhead. Its area overhead is as small as 38% of the fixed-point datapath, and the critical path delay is 6 ns in 0.25 /spl mu/m CMOS technology, which makes it well suited to modern audio applications such as MP3 and AAC. The floating-point unit is verified through an efficient test vector generation method developed to reduce verification time significantly.

title: Investigation of delay compensation circuit techniques to reduce timing walk
authors: Haiming Yu; R.S. Miyaoka; T.K. Lewellen
venue: 1998 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium Conference Record. 1998 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference (Cat. No.98CH36255)
abstract: Two methods are investigated to reduce the timing walk for an integrated ASIC chip to less than 1 ns without requiring an offchip delay line. In each method a delay compensation circuit is used to adjust the position of the timing marker dependent upon the size of the input signal. For signals with identical rise times a large signal will usually generate its timing pulse faster than a small signal. The first circuit is added to a monolithic constant fraction discriminator (CFD). Using one control signal based on the input signal size, an analog delay is used to delay the zero-crossing signal to the comparator for signals above a certain threshold. After analog delay compensation, the timing walk of the CFD is 660 ps or 54% of the value of the CFD without analog compensation for a signal size range of 10. The second circuit is added to a simple leading-edge discriminator. The circuit uses digital delay lines, where the length of the delay is based on the size of the input signal. The timing walk is reduced by 83%, from 4.05 ns (without digital compensation) to 700 ps (with digital compensation) for a signal size range of 8.

title: A Mathematical Model for the Estimation of Treatment Cost in Cancer Radiotherapy
authors: Suzi Wahl; Tanísia Foletto; Gerson Feldmann
abstract: In this work we present a methodology for the investigation of costs of cancer treatment by radiotherapy, aiming to reduce the undesired effects of radiation and to obtain better results of the treatment. The tumor growth is simulated by using a mathematical model composed of three ordinary diferential equations corresponding to the population of Normal (N), Tumoral (T) and Imune (I) cells. The effect of radiation over each type of cells is considered using the linear quadratic model applied for the various distinct treatment protocols investigated. Cost of treatment is obtained using a model based on the concept of tumor cure probability, cost per fraction and cost of failure. The concept of biological effective dose is used in order to compare differente treatment protocols. We investigated different protocols currently used for various tumor types. Our results show that with this approach it is possible to obtain more efficient protocols with lower cost that those used. It is also possible to investigate the effect of fractionation protocols on the tumor evolution in order to obtain less aggressive protocols that are effective for patient cure with lower total dose and in smaller treatment time.

title: Input ordering in concurrent checkers to reduce power consumption
venue: 17th IEEE International Symposium on Defect and Fault Tolerance in VLSI Systems, 2002. DFT 2002. Proceedings.
abstract: A novel approach for reducing power consumption in checkers used for concurrent error detection is presented. Spatial correlations between the outputs of the circuit that drives the primary inputs of the checker are analyzed to order them such that switching activity (and hence power consumption) in the checker is minimized. The reduction in power consumption comes at no additional impact to area or performance and does not require any alteration to the design flow. Since the number of possible input orders increases exponentially in the number of inputs to the checker, the computational costs of determining the optimum order can be very expensive. We present a very effective technique to build a reduced cost function to solve the optimization problem to find a near optimal order.

title: Symmetric And Asymmetric Algorithms for Susceptible Harmful in Wireless Sensor Network on FPGA Platform
authors: L. Saranya; C. Arvind; Zhu; Seng Tang
venue: 2023 9th International Conference on Advanced Computing and Communication Systems (ICACCS)
abstract: WSNs are made up of a network of sensor nodes that are used to track environmental characteristics like pressure, temperature, etc. and communicate the data to the intended location. Networks must overcome obstacles including security, routing, problems with energy conservation, scalability, dependability, secrecy, integrity, authentication, and others when transmitting information. Different routing systems, including data-centric, location- and mobility-based, Quality of Service (QoS)-based, and multipath routing protocols, have been employed to address these issues. Even while these routing methods guarantee a successful transaction, the network still has to manage intermediary assaults that can completely alter the content of messages being carried. Therefore, a number of cryptographic approaches have been used to minimise the network. The newly developed symmetric and asymmetric algorithms are susceptible to problems with route latency, area overhead, and on-chip power consumption. Thus, to reduce these harmful actions in WSNs, an efficient reduced key size and high security based cryptographic method must be used. Utilizing the limited network resources, the main goal of the study is to increase network security while reducing network overhead and path delay-related problems.

title: Optimal outsourcing for intellectual property protection and production cost minimization
authors: John P Kim; Karim Hamza; Kazuhiro Saitou
venue: 2009 IEEE International Symposium on Assembly and Manufacturing
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for optimal outsourcing of products. Outsourcing of products can have the advantage of reducing the production cost, but often causes a risk that important technology may leak and get used by competitors. To help reduce the risk of intellectual property (IP) leakage, a model proposed in this paper assumes that it is possible to separate some of the important geometrical features on some of the product parts that are outsourced, and then manufacture them in-house. The model estimates the fraction of IP-value that is subject to risk of leakage based on patent claims and how they relate to the outsourced parts and/or features. Production cost is modelled by assuming a base cost for manufacturing parts in-house, and then a discount rate is applied if the decision to outsource is made. Separation of geometrical features from manufactured parts introduces additional cost, which is modelled as an overhead if the decision to separate features is made. The outsourcing management process is then viewed as a two-objective problem, with the objectives being the minimization of both the fraction of IP-value at risk of leakage, as well as the production cost. A case study of an auto-slide-hinge mechanism is presented, in which the two-objective optimization problem is transformed into a single-objective constrained problem. Genetic algorithm is then applied iteratively on the problem in order generate the Pareto-plot that visualizes the trade-offs between the two objectives.

title: Utilization Analysis of a Hybrid Power Plant in Sangihe Islands to Decrease the Cost of Supply and Carbon Emission Rate
venue: 2024 International Conference on Technology and Policy in Energy and Electric Power (ICTPEP)
abstract: To contribute to the electricity sector's energy transition program, PT PLN (Persero) continues to increase the renewable energy mix to meet customer demand, particularly through the de-dieselization program in remote areas and islands. This involves utilizing local renewable energy potential, including hybrid power plants. The fuel cost for the Sangihe Island electricity system remains high, with an average biodiesel/HSD requirement in 2022 of 8,198,343 liters/year, equivalent to Rp. 88,115,790,564 billion annually. Thus, renewable energy is an alternative to reduce operational costs from diesel generator fuel. Additionally, hybridizing diesel generators with solar power plants can increase efficiency and reduce carbon emissions from an environmental sustainability perspective. This paper discusses the effect of operating a 1.3 MW peak hybrid solar power plant in the Sangihe Islands, North Sulawesi Province, to achieve efficiency by reducing supply costs and carbon emissions, analyzing calculations according to IPCC 2006 through direct data collection. The Sangihe solar power plant began operating in July 2022. From January to December 2023, the Sangihe electricity system produced 30,104,354 kWh, with 1,251,759 kWh from the solar power plant, resulting in fuel savings of 355,500 liters, equivalent to Rp. 5,046,494,028. During January-December 2023, a Renewable Fraction of 4.15% was obtained, and the carbon emission rate was reduced to 960,149 tons C02.

title: Power dispatching in microgrids considering the cost of Hydrogen-Based power generation
authors: Tan Loc Luu; Chau Le Thi Minh; Hai Pham Hong; My Hien Nguyen Thi; Hieu Nguyen Hoang Xuan; Tu Duc Nguyen
venue: 2025 Asia Meeting on Environment and Electrical Engineering (EEE-AM)
abstract: This paper proposes a power dispatch method for a biomass–hydrogen integrated microgrid, considering economic, technical, and environmental aspects. A hybrid gas turbine model fueled by methane (CH4) from a biomass plant and hydrogen (H2) is developed on the Brayton cycle framework using Aspen HYSYS, with input parameters calibrated from real-world data. The generation cost of the biomass unit is modeled using a quadratic cost function, while the hydrogen price is represented by a time-of-use (TOU) tariff to capture energy market variability. Several operating scenarios are investigated to minimize the cost objective function and to analyze the impact of the hydrogen blending ratio on power output, CO2 emissions, and turbine inlet temperature (TIT). The results show that increasing the hydrogen share from 0% to 100% raises the power output from 3.973 MW to 11.053 MW, while CO2 emissions decrease from 2.743 ton/h to zero. However, TIT rises from 958.6°C to 1615°C, imposing constraints related to material strength and cooling requirements. The cost analysis indicates that the optimal hydrogen fraction depends on TOU pricing, enabling a trade-off between economic performance and emission reduction. The proposed dispatch strategy identifies the optimal hydrogen share under both cost and technical constraints, ensuring safe operation while reducing CO2 emissions. These findings provide a techno-economic basis for the development of low-carbon biomass–hydrogen microgrids

title: Reducing energy consumption, operation cost, environmental impact for LPG separation unity, by using process energy integration
venue: 2016 International Renewable and Sustainable Energy Conference (IRSEC)
abstract: The Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) separation unit is one of process, in chemical industries that consume great energy. In this work, Pinch technology for heat recovery is used to minimize the energy consumption of the LPG separation process, for a Moroccan oil refinery. This methodology was applied to the study of the separation of LPG, using the two distillation columns: recovery and splitter columns. Experimental data required to follow this method, were obtained from Moroccan oil refinery, during period of May 2015. To find the optimal energetic integration, the different calculations were performed by simulation, using PRO II software. Results analyses show that the integration of three heat exchangers in conventional process reduces the energy consumption of process, operation cost and decreases the impact environment.

title: A Generic Circuit Platform of Covering All Rational Numbers for Determnistic Stochastic Computing in the Time Dimension
authors: Xiangye Wei; Junjian Ma; Liming Xiu; Yimao Cai
venue: 2025 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The key advantages of stochastic computing (SC) are its simple arithmetic circuits and high tolerance for bit errors. Deterministic SC (DSC) improves SC by using deterministic bitstreams, resulting in accurate results without fluctuation. Recently, a platform that conducts DSC in the time domain has been proposed. This platform enhances the feasibility of DSC and brings it closer to becoming a mainstream computational paradigm. However, its circuit is unable to represent all rational numbers. This work improves the platform by enabling the representation of all rational numbers for computation. Furthermore, it reduces hardware costs and power consumption, paving the way for new SC applications.

title: Optimized decision delays in finite-length MIMO DFE
authors: Hai Huyen Dam.; S. Nordholm; G. Day
abstract: Finite-length multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) decision feedback equalizers (DFEs) that optimize the decision delays are investigated herein. The mean square error (MSE) of each output with respect to the decision delays is derived to form the basis of the optimization cost function. A genetic algorithm (GA) is implemented to reduce the computational burden of the search. Simulation results show that the GA successfully tracks the optimum decision delays with only a fraction of the computational complexity of the global search. Moreover, the use of optimized decision delays in the MIMO DFE for simulated fading MIMO channels provides an average improvement of 4.1 dB for the combined output MSE.

title: Delay-dependent synchronization stability for delayed complex dynamical networks with stochastic coupling
venue: Proceedings of the 31st Chinese Control Conference
abstract: The synchronization stability problem is investigated for a class of stochastic complex dynamical network with time delay. In order to reduce the conservatism, the delay is divided into several segments, by employing a novel delay-segment-dependent Lyapunov functional, some new delay-dependent synchronization stability conditions are derived in terms of linear matrix inequalities, which can be solved efficiently by the LMI toolbox. This new criteria based on a delay fractioning approach can reduce the conservation as the delay fractioning number increases. A numerical example is provided to show the advantage of the proposed techniques.

title: Optimal-Cost Reachability Analysis Based on Time Petri Nets
authors: Hanifa Boucheneb; Didier Lime; Olivier H. Roux; Charlotte Seidner
venue: 2018 18th International Conference on Application of Concurrency to System Design (ACSD)
abstract: This paper investigates the optimal-cost reachability problem in the context of time Petri nets, where a rate cost is associated with each place. This problem consists in deciding whether or not a given goal marking is reachable and providing, in case it is reachable, a sequence leading at lower cost to the goal marking. This paper shows that for some subclasses of cost time Petri nets, the optimal-cost reachability problem can be solved more efficiently using a method based on the state classes, without resorting to linear programming or splitting state classes.

title: Parallel test reduces cost of test more effectively than just a cheap tester
venue: IEEE/CPMT/SEMI 29th International Electronics Manufacturing Technology Symposium (IEEE Cat. No.04CH37585)
abstract: Today's manufacturers of high-volume consumer devices are under tremendous cost pressure and consequently under extreme pressure to reduce cost of test. Low-cost ATE has often been promoted as the obvious solution. Parallel test is another well-known approach, where multiple devices are tested in parallel (multi-site test) and/or multiple blocks within one device are tested in parallel (concurrent test). This paper shows quantitatively that parallel test is a much effective test cost reduction method than low-cost ATE, because it reduces all test cost contributors, not only capital cost of ATE. It also shows that the optimum number of sites is relatively insensitive to ATE capital cost, operating cost, yield, and various limiting factors, but the cost benefits diminish fast, if limited independent ATE resources reduce the degree of parallelism and force a partially sequential test.

title: Fractional delay compensation in digital predistortion system
authors: Hao Huang; Hua Qian; Hui Xu; Xiaotao Wang
venue: 2012 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
abstract: Delay mismatch between the input and output signals of power amplifiers (PAs) may lead to an erroneous assumption of memory effects. In adaptive digital predistortion (DPD) system, the delay mismatch affects the accuracy of coefficients estimation and degrades performance of the DPD system. In this paper, we reveal the impact of fractional delay mismatch, and analyze the relationship between delay mismatch and memory effects. The fractional delay compensation helps to reduce or eliminate the delay mismatch. Benefits of fractional delay compensation are provided through numerical analysis and experimental results.

title: Design and Verification of a Fractional Delay Implementation Scheme for Wireless Communication Channel Simulation
authors: Kai Han; Lv Ping; Ting Chen; Rui Cao; Zhaohui Wang; Yixin You
venue: 2025 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computer Networks and Communications (SPCNC)
abstract: Channel simulation is a key link in the design and testing of wireless communication systems, and accurate multipath delay control directly affects the authenticity of simulation results. Traditional integer delay implementation (based on shift registers or circular buffers) cannot meet the demand for non-integer sampling period delay in complex channels, leading to phase distortion of high-frequency signals. To solve this problem, this paper has two core contributions: (1) A low-resource linear interpolation design is adopted for the fractional delay module, which only requires 2 multipliers and 1 adder, significantly reducing hardware resource consumption compared with state-of-the-art methods. (2) The scheme balances resource efficiency and delay accuracy, and is suitable for real-time wireless channel simulation scenarios. Experimental results show that it has low hardware resource consumption and high delay accuracy (the delay error is less than 0.05 sampling periods for narrowband signals and less than 0.1 sampling periods for wideband signals), with signal distortion degree (evaluated by EVM) less than $3 \%$, which can effectively simulate the multipath channel characteristics of wireless communication systems.

title: Optimization and Feasibility Analysis of a Grid-Connected Hybrid Renewable Microgrid for Cost and Emission Reduction in Bangladesh
authors: Rasel Islam; Md Abu Yousuf; M Shaharyar Alam; MD. Asraful Mursalin Jesun; Md. Mehedi Hasan
venue: 2026 International Conference on Power, Electronics, Communications, Computing, and Intelligent Infrastructure (PECCII)
abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable and reliable energy systems has accelerated the integration of renewable energy technologies to reduce fossil fuel dependency and grid instability. This paper presents the design and techno-economic optimization of a grid-connected PV–Wind–Battery Energy Storage System microgrid for an educational institution in Bangladesh. The proposed system is modelled and optimized using HOMER Pro to evaluate its economic, environmental and operational performance. Simulation results indicate that the optimized hybrid microgrid reduces the Net Present Cost by 65% to $45,085 and the Cost of Energy by 75% to $0.0246/kWh compared to the existing grid-only system. The proposed system achieves an 84% renewable energy fraction and decreases annual CO2 emissions by 75.3%. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis with ±40% variation in key technical and economic parameters confirms the robustness and financial viability of the proposed system. The findings demonstrate that grid-connected hybrid microgrids provide a cost-effective, reliable, and sustainable solution for institutional energy management in Bangladesh.

title: Performance of non-delay-line constant-fraction discriminator timing circuits
abstract: The delay line in the constant-fraction discriminator (CFD) can be replaced with circuit networks to permit monolithic fabrication. The previously reported non-delay-line CFD utilizing a single-pole highpass filter is reviewed, followed by a presentation of non-delay-line circuits utilizing Gaussian lowpass filters. Circuit response for non-delay-line CFDs utilizing single-pole highpass or single-pole lowpass filters is shown to be equivalent. However, timing-signal underdrive and zero-crossing slope are increased and timing jitter reduced when higher-order lowpass filters are used. Comparisons of non-delay-line and delay-line CFD circuit timing performance are presented for lowpass-filtered step inputs representative of scintillation detector signals. Timing resolution of non-delay-line and delay-line CFDs is compared for BGO/photomultiplier scintillation detector applications. Monte Carlo simulations indicate that comparable timing resolution is available with proper selection of non-delay-line CFD filter time-constants. A fully-monolithic CMOS, non-delay-line CFD was fabricated to experimentally validate timing resolution. The measured timing resolution of 3.26 ns FWHM and 6.5 ns FWTM is in good agreement with measured resolution of 3.30 ns FWHM and 6.4 ns FWTM for a standard delay-line CFD circuit.<>

title: Application of Compensating Conductors to Reduce the Impact of Magnetic Field from the Power Lines on the Main Pipelines
authors: Julia V. Mokrousova; Alexander A. Myulbaer
venue: 2018 XIV International Scientific-Technical Conference on Actual Problems of Electronics Instrument Engineering (APEIE)
abstract: The paper touches upon the problem of protection of pipeline systems for transportation of raw materials from the destructive effect of the voltage induced by the overhead AC power transmission lines. The authors propose a new method of reducing the negative impact of the overhead power transmission lines, i.e. application of compensating conductor, which is quite effective and does not require special technical control being an economical way of pipelines protection. The method of increasing the efficiency of compensating conductor application is also suggested.

title: New Delay-Dependent Exponential Stability for Neural Networks With Time Delay
authors: Shaoshuai Mou; Huijun Gao; Wenyi Qiang; Ke Chen
venue: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics, Part B (Cybernetics)
abstract: In this correspondence, the problem of exponential stability for neural networks with time delay is investigated. By introducing a novel Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional with the idea of delay fractioning, a new criterion of exponential stability is derived and then formulated in terms of a linear matrix inequality. This new criterion proves to be much less conservative than the most recent result, and the conservatism can be notably reduced as the fractioning goes thinner. An example is provided to demonstrate the advantage of the proposed result.

title: Delay macromodels for point-to-point MCM interconnections
venue: IEEE Transactions on Components, Packaging, and Manufacturing Technology: Part B
abstract: We develop delay macromodels for lossless as well as lossy point-to-point MCM transmission lines using a systematic model construction procedure that includes dimensional analysis. The result for lossless lines confirms earlier work and extends it to the case of nonlinear drivers and capacitive termination. For lossy lines, we show that dimensional analysis allows us to reduce the complexity of the delay expression without any loss in accuracy. A second-order polynomial fit to a four-argument delay function is shown to yield predictions that are within 5% of detailed circuit simulation at a fraction of the computational cost. We illustrate the applications of these macromodels in studying the effects of packaging technology on signal delay and in sensitivity analysis.<>

title: On the overhead-delay tradeoff in carrier sense collision channels
venue: Proceedings. International Symposium on Information Theory, 2005. ISIT 2005.
abstract: In this paper, we study the impact of delay constraints on the throughput of a queued multiple-access system. We model the channel as a collision channel with carrier sense to capture the inherent information sharing due to broadcast nature of the wireless channels. Since the queue state information is unknown to other nodes and a delay-bounded communication is desired, we show that a fraction of throughput is lost as protocol overhead. More importantly, we show that there is a tradeoff between protocol overhead and queuing delay; larger delays allowing smaller overheads. In addition, we show that larger network loads can also be used to reduce protocol overhead, which is in direct contrast of the behavior exhibited by commonly used medium access protocols

title: Reducing Communication Overhead of Key Distribution Schemes for Wireless Sensor Networks
venue: 2007 16th International Conference on Computer Communications and Networks
abstract: Establishing a secure communication link in a wireless sensor network is a challenging task due to resource limitation and wireless nature of transmission. A symmetric key distribution is a practical and efficient solution which has been studied extensively [4][5][6][7][9][11]. A secure communication link is established between sensors that hold common keys, which are discovered by each node broadcasting the key identifiers of its key ring. We make modifications to existing schemes to reduce communication overhead during the key discovery phase. This is achieved without weakening network connectivity or system resiliency against key compromise. We also introduce families of new deterministic key distribution schemes with low-communication overhead.

title: CFD Analysis Of Hydrodynamics And Oil-Water Separation In Surface-Enhanced Quartz Granular Filtration Systems
venue: JOURNAL OF APPLIED SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING
abstract: Understanding hydrodynamic behaviour within granular filtration systems is critical for optimizing oil-water separation performance. This study presents a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis of flow characteristics and multiphase interactions in surface-enhanced quartz granular filtration systems. The model is developed based on the Navier-Stokes equations coupled with a Volume of Fluid (VOF) approach and a porous media framework to simulate the transport and separation of oil-water mixtures under varying operating conditions. The simulation results reveal that flow within the granular bed is inherently non-uniform, with localized high-velocity regions near the inlet reducing residence time and limiting effective separation. In contrast, reduced velocities along the filtration bed enhance fluid-surface interaction, promoting improved oil removal. The CFD results, interpreted in conjunction with experimentally validated wettability data, indicate that surface-enhanced quartz promotes improved fluid-surface interaction and enhanced separation performance. The pressure distribution indicates a gradual pressure drop along the bed height, consistent with porous media flow behaviour and indicative of stable, energy-efficient operation. The oil volume fraction analysis further confirms progressive phase separation, with significant reduction in oil concentration along the flow path. The findings highlight the critical role of hydrodynamic conditions and surface engineering in governing oil-water separation efficiency. This study provides a CFD-based framework for understanding internal flow mechanisms and supports the design and optimization of cost-effective, scalable, and energy-efficient granular filtration systems for industrial wastewater treatment.

title: FDASR-PINNs: A feature-enhanced dual-head physics-informed neural network for sparse-data liquid hydrogen dispersion prediction
authors: Wang, Chengyang; Jiang, Shangfeng; Tao, Ting; Zhao, Shichang; Xie, An; Zeng, Sheng
abstract: Liquid hydrogen (LH2) leakage produces cryogenic plumes with sharp, coupled concentration and temperature gradients that are difficult to reconstruct from sparse observations. High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) remains computationally expensive for transient consequence analysis, and a standard physics-informed neural network (PINN) struggles with multiscale structures, coupled outputs, imbalanced constraints, and evolving high-residual regions. This study develops a feature-enhanced dual-head physics-informed neural network with adaptive weighting, staged training and residual refinement (FDASR-PINNs) to reconstruct coupled multiscale concentration-temperature fields in a reduced two-dimensional center-plane setting. Fourier/radialbasis-function (RBF) feature lifting improves the representation of sharp plume structures, while separate physics-constrained output heads reconstruct hydrogen mass fraction and temperature. Adaptive loss weighting, staged Adam/L-BFGS training, and residual-based resampling stabilize optimization under sparse supervision. The model is evaluated against CFD-derived no-wind and wind benchmarks using 10-50 % of the training data. With 10% of the training data, FDASR-PINNs achieves a wind-case temperature root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 37.7 K, compared with 48.2 K for a standard PINN and 47.7 K for a data-only deep neural network (DNN). In the no-wind concentration case, the RMSE is 3.89 & times;10-2, compared with 4.15 & times;10-2 for the standard PINN and 4.88 & times;10-2 for the DNN. The results support CFD-benchmark screening for unobstructed, approximately symmetric, near-ground releases during the simulated interval, but they do not establish performance for threedimensional, multiphase, obstacle-dominated, or experimentally measured releases.

title: Biorefining of whole cotton plant residues for bioethanol production with greenhouse gas emission reduction and social carbon benefits
authors: Salehi, Danial; Zilouei, Hamid; Denayer, Joeri F. M.; Okoro, Oseweuba Valentine; Shahvandi, Armin; Karimi, Keikhosro
abstract: This study evaluated the potential of cotton-processing residues, including leaves, bolls, linters, and stalks, as feedstocks for bioethanol production using ethanol-based organosolv pretreatment. Biomass samples were pretreated with 65 % (v/v) ethanol at 120, 150, and 180 degrees C for 30 and 60 min, followed by enzymatic hydrolysis and fermentation. Organosolv pretreatment altered biomass composition through partial removal of hemicellulose and enrichment of glucan in the recovered solids, which was associated with improved enzymatic digestibility and ethanol production. The highest hydrolysis efficiencies reached 75.4 %, 80.2 %, 83.0 %, and 79.9 % for leaves, bolls, linters, and stalks, respectively. Correspondingly, the highest ethanol yields were obtained from leaves (70.8 %) and stalks (61.1 %) after pretreatment at 180 degrees C for 30 min, while maximum yields of 42.3 % and 42.6 % were achieved for bolls and linters, respectively. The results demonstrated that pretreatment severity significantly influenced both hydrolysis and fermentation performance, although the optimal conditions varied among biomass fractions. Greenhouse gas reduction calculations estimated that replacing gasoline with E85, E10, and E5 ethanol-gasoline blends could reduce emissions by 55.7 %, 4.9 %, and 2.4 %, respectively. In addition, the social cost of carbon analysis indicated substantial reductions in the social cost of carbon emissions, with the highest benefit obtained from boll-derived bioethanol due to its greater production potential. These findings demonstrate that cotton-processing residues represent a promising lignocellulosic resource for bioethanol production while supporting agricultural waste valorization and greenhouse gas mitigation.

title: Glycerol-assisted co-solvothermal liquefaction of food waste: Investigation of biocrude's fuel properties with proposed reaction mechanisms
abstract: The conversion of biowaste into biofuels has garnered attention in recent years due to the pressing need for sustainable energy solutions in the US. Owing to the rising volume of food waste (FW), producing biofuel from FW can address both waste management issues and provide a sustainable fuel alternative. Solvothermal liquefaction (STL) is a proven cutting-edge thermochemical pathway for producing biocrude oil from biowaste, potentially reducing dependence on fossil fuels. In addition, owing to low cost and ability to act as an in-situ hydrogen donor that stabilizes reactive intermediates, glycerol has potential as a liquefaction solvent. Prior work on co-solvent studies is typically based on one or two arbitrarily selected co-solvent loadings, which cannot distinguish a genuine synergistic optimum from a monotonic trend, and the influence of solvent composition remains unresolved. This study, therefore, examines the co-solvothermal liquefaction (Co-STL) of FW across the full glycerol-water composition range, from pure glycerol to pure water, to determine how solvent composition governs biocrude yield and quality. In this study, glycerol and water were mixed at ratios of 1:0, 3:1, 1:1, 1:3, and 0:1 (v/v), and the Co-STL was performed at 280-320 degrees C for 30 min. For all experiments, a 1:10 (w/v) FW-tosolvent ratio was maintained. The maximum amount of biocrude was obtained at 320 degrees C (50.06 +/- 3.96 wt%), with a heating value of 34.15 +/- 0.55 MJ/kg, utilizing solely glycerol as the solvent. The thermogravimetric analysis revealed that biocrude obtained from water-based liquefaction contained a higher proportion of light fractions, e.g., gasoline/naphtha, kerosene, and diesel, compared to pure glycerol solvolysis. According to the GC-MS report, the produced biocrude is primarily composed of hydrocarbons, ketones, aldehydes, phenols, esters, alcohols, nitrogen-containing compounds, and organic acids. Based on ex-situ GC-MS and FT-IR analysis, reaction mechanisms for biocrude formation at varying glycerol concentrations were proposed. The findings indicate that STL is a promising and sustainable technology for converting FW into biocrude, aiding in advancing bioeconomy goals.

title: Papers Power grid support from battery storage paired with solar panels under lower compensation for electricity exports
authors: Aldaadi, Mohsen; Verbic, Gregor; Zhang, Cuo
abstract: Distributed photovoltaic (PV)-battery portfolios can reshape bulk-system operation under net billing, yet their schedules reflect prosumer rather than system objectives. This study develops an export-enabled bilevel production cost model (PCM) coupling transmission-constrained unit commitment with aggregated prosumer virtual power plants (P-VPPs). Each P-VPP solves a continuous linear program under asymmetric import and export remuneration. Strict import-export coefficient ordering makes optimal grid exchange direction-exclusive, allowing exact lower-level embedding through primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and strong duality. This yields a mixed-integer linear program (MILP). A complete-year rolling-horizon study on an Australian National Electricity Market-inspired system compares matched sequential and integrated formulations across battery and remuneration scenarios. Across battery-enabled cases, integrated selection among P-VPP-optimal schedules reduces annual production cost by 2.74%-7.08% relative to the sequential benchmark, peak scheduled net demand by 0.81-2.02 GW, and mean absolute hourly variation by 10.9%-62.0%. It also raises utility-scale variable renewable energy utilisation by 1.50-3.42 percentage points and reduces synchronous-unit starts by approximately 13%-50%. The best-performing P-VPP case reduces annual production cost by 23.6% relative to the conventional PCM reference without the P-VPP portfolio; this combined effect includes distributed PV, storage, remuneration, and integrated selection. Under the optimistic selection convention, the integrated formulation provides an optimistic rolling-horizon benchmark while preserving P-VPP optimality. Larger batteries increase absolute storage use but reduce the fraction of centralised incremental production-cost value realised, showing that system value depends jointly on capacity, remuneration, and schedule-selection architecture.

title: Microbial bioleaching for critical metal recovery from E-waste: mechanistic advances, process integration and circular economy readiness
authors: Halder, Banhi; Sampath, Muthu Kumar; Nigam, Vinod Kumar
venue: JOURNAL OF MATERIAL CYCLES AND WASTE MANAGEMENT
abstract: Electronic waste (e-waste) represents one of the fastest-growing solid waste streams globally, generating 62 million tonnes in 2022 alone, only 22.3% of e-waste was formally collected and recycled. Printed circuit boards (PCBs), which constitute the most metal-rich fraction of e-waste, contain recoverable concentrations of copper (10-20%), tin (1-3%), and precious metals including gold (0.03-0.3%), yet conventional pyrometallurgical and hydrometallurgical processing routes impose prohibitive energy demands, generate toxic secondary emissions, and are poorly suited to the compositional heterogeneity of post-consumer PCBs. Bioleaching utilizes microorganisms and their metabolites to extract metals from solid materials, emerging as a lower-energy, lower-emission, and scalable alternative. However, the field lacks a comprehensive synthesis addressing mechanistic understanding, engineering constraints, sustainability, and commercial viability. Bioleaching reduces greenhouse gas emissions by 18-39% compared to pyrometallurgy. In configurations where bioleaching directly substitutes mineral-acid-based hydrometallurgical, reported copper production costs are about 47% lower than conventional processing. Integrated bioleaching-electrochemical recovery has achieved over 99% copper recovery following biological solubilization of multilayer industrial waste under reported conditions. This finding support circular economy integration, although many innovative techniques remain below technology readiness level 5 (TRL 5). This review critically examines microbial bioleaching of e-waste metals, highlighting mechanistic advances, sustainability assessments, commercialization challenges, and future strategies for scalable and digitally integrated bioprocessing.

title: NOVA-HOI: Notions From Oracles for Verb-Agnostic HOI Detection
authors: Zancani, Lea; Sabourin, Astrid; Luvison, Bertrand
abstract: Human-Object Interaction (HOI) detection has long been constrained to fixed sets of predefined interaction categories, limiting generalization to novel verbs and unseen verb-object combinations. While recent work addresses this through zero-shot protocols that partition HICO-DET into seen and unseen categories, this approach is self-defeating: withholding interaction categories from an already data-scarce task reduces training diversity, which is precisely what generic verb understanding requires. This limitation is particularly acute for lightweight models trained exclusively on supervised HOI data, which are structurally disadvantaged relative to VLM (Vision Language Model)-based architectures that implicitly benefit from web-scale pretraining, making zero-shot splits an uneven basis for comparison. Moreover, VLM-based architectures are generally more resource-intensive. Very few methods address genuine open-vocabulary scenarios that evaluate models across different datasets with potentially different verb semantics without sacrificing training data. However, MLLMs (Multi-modal Large Language Models) offer large-vocabulary capabilities but they struggle with accurate interaction localization, are prone to relation hallucination, and are computationally prohibitive for practical applications. In this paper, we propose NOVA-HOI, a teacher-student framework that leverages MLLMs' description capabilities to pseudo-annotate new data for HOI detection. Crucially, we leverage these models exclusively for offline HOI annotation generation, while maintaining a lightweight detector suitable for practical deployment. Our teacher-student framework integrates these pseudo-annotations using a novel semantic filter, enabling training of an open-verb HOI detector. To rigorously evaluate unseen verb capabilities, we introduce HICOCO, a new evaluation dataset featuring 131 novel verbs and 310 novel HOI classes that systematically tests generalization to unseen interactions beyond HICO-DET. Direct cross-dataset transfer validates our method's open-vocabulary HOI detection capability, achieving state-of-the-art results with + 4 percentage points mAP role (scenario 2) on V-COCO and + 7 mAP on HICOCO, while remaining competitive with closed-set expert models at a fraction of their computational cost. HICOCO annotations are publicly available at https://github.com/ CEA-LIST/HICOCO

title: Substrate Attachment Voids and Their Impact on VSWR/Insertion Loss Performance for Low-Power Passive Circuits
authors: Tripathi, Shivendra; Sarode, Anuj; Kumar, Satendra; Sharma, Deepak Kumar; Singh, Harimohan; Sinha, Santanu; Prajapati, Ishwarlal
venue: IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON COMPONENTS PACKAGING AND MANUFACTURING TECHNOLOGY
abstract: Substrate-attachment voids are critical defects in high-reliability RF assemblies, yet their quantitative impact on passive circuit performance is underreported. This study correlates Au80Sn20 solder voiding with the simulated voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) and measured insertion loss (IL) of miniature hybrid semi-monolithic microstrip lines and bandpass filters (BPF) across C through Ka band. Full-wave 3-D FEM (Ansys HFSS) and MoM planar EM (Keysight ADS Momentum) simulations were validated experimentally on microstrip-line and BPF test vehicles (TVs), respectively. Across void fractions from 4.3% to 44.9%, insertion loss showed no correlation with void content; the largest post-bake deviation observed was -0.33 dB, bounding any void-related effect below that level. A 144-h bake at 125 C-degrees confirmed electrical stability, with minor fluctuations tied to stress relaxation. The results support distinguishing active-device thermal paths from passive ground paths, avoiding unnecessary rework and reducing manufacturing costs.

title: Spatial variation of roadside soil quality and its key influencing factors on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau
authors: Gong, Lin; Ma, Wencan; Wen, Xingyue
abstract: Investigation on the soil quality and its influencing factors along the highways of the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau holds significant value for understanding the ecological environment of high-altitude regions. Principal component analysis was utilized to identify the minimum dataset and establish a soil quality index evaluation system based on physicochemical property indicators of surface soil samples collected from road-side locations in representative areas of the Plateau. By integrating spatial zoning and altitude gradient analysis, this study reveals the spatial variations in soil quality both horizontally and vertically. The results show that the final minimum dataset comprised soil organic matter, total phosphorus, C/N ratio, and N/P ratio, which effectively reflected regional soil quality variances; soil organic matter carried the highest weight and acted as the primary evaluation indicator. Clear spatial disparities in soil quality were evident: values were relatively elevated in the eastern and southern plateau but lower in western and northern regions. Along altitudinal gradients, soil quality reached its peak at middle elevations (3200-4500 m) and decreased at low (2700-3100 m) and high elevations (4500-5100 m). Precipitation, temperature, and vegetation types along altitudinal gradients mainly governed soil quality variability by controlling litter input, microbial decomposition, and soil organic matter accumulation, with soil organic matter playing a crucial role as a key mediator linking environmental gradients to soil quality shifts. The proposed SQI-MDS framework effectively characterizes soil quality variations with fewer indicators and reduced survey costs, offering scientific support for large-scale soil resource monitoring and ecological environment management on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau.

title: Development and performance testing of a high-sensitivity pulsed flame photometric detector
authors: Chen, Junbin; Cai, Haoyuan; Deng, Zhihan; Jin, Yujie; Sun, Jianhai
abstract:
The conventional flame photometric detector (FPD) is widely used for sulfur-selective gas chromatography. However, the FPD is sensitive to hydrocarbon backgrounds. Its sulfur response also depends strongly on flame stability. These factors limit stable trace sulfur determination in complex matrices. A pulsed flame photometric detector (PFPD) provides a time-resolved approach to this problem. Sulfur emission appears later than most hydrocarbon background emissions after pulsed combustion. A suitable acquisition window can therefore improve sulfur selectivity. In this study, a high-sensitivity single-channel PFPD was designed and tested. The aim was to establish reproducible operating conditions for trace sulfur analysis. The detector consisted of five functional modules: the combustion and ignition module, the gas supply module, the optical collection and detection module, the temperature-control module, and the mechanical support and sealing module. The combustion zone consisted of a vertically mounted quartz chamber. The chamber had an outer diameter of 4 mm. Its inner diameter was 2 mm. Its total length was 17.5 mm. The effective combustion length was 12 mm. The calculated chamber volume was 37.68 mm3. Numerical simulation was used to examine flame propagation and self-extinction. A 12 mm effective length maintained a stable finger-shaped flame front. The flame was self-terminated near the lower limiting orifice at about 1.97 ms. The hydroxyl radical mass fraction decreased close to baseline within 5 ms, whereas the temperature decayed more gradually and approached its initial level at approximately 30 ms. These results supported the chamber design for periodic pulsed combustion. The optical unit used a quartz light guide and a BG-12 band-pass filter. The filter matched the sulfur emission band near 394 nm. A photomultiplier tube (PMT) recorded the time-resolved emission signal. Two electronic pneumatic control (EPC) units were used for gas regulation. One unit controlled hydrogen and air for the ignition chamber. The other unit controlled hydrogen and air for the combustion chamber. This design separated ignition conditions from analytical combustion conditions. It also reduced uncertainty caused by coupled gas adjustment. The optimization started with the ignition chamber. Then the combustion chamber was optimized under the fixed ignition baseline. Finally, detector temperature and PMT voltage were evaluated. Peak area, sensitivity, and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) were used as indicators. Gas chromatographic tests used a sulfur-specific quartz capillary column. Nitrogen was used as the carrier gas. The gate delay was 6 ms. The gate width was 18 ms. The trigger level was 500 mV. A stable pulsed flame was obtained at an ignition-chamber hydrogen flow of 8.0 mL/min. The corresponding ignition-chamber air flow was 19.0 mL/min. Under this ignition baseline, the combustion chamber was further adjusted. A higher sulfur response was obtained at 5.0 mL/min hydrogen. The corresponding air flow was 3.7 mL/min. Detector temperature also affected the delayed sulfur emission. The response was low at 110-130 degrees C.At about 150 degrees C, the delayed sulfur signal was higher. Peak area and sulfur sensitivity were also higher at this temperature. Higher temperatures from 170 to 250 degrees C reduced the peak area and sensitivity. PMT voltage affected signal amplitude, SNR, and waveform fidelity. Increasing the voltage from 590 to 710 V improved the SNR. At 730 V, the delayed emission plateau showed peak clipping.

This behavior indicated saturation or nonlinear response in the detection chain. Dynamic dilutions of a 10 mu mol/mol hydrogen sulfide (H2S) standard gas were used to evaluate the linear range. A 1.1 mu mol/mol H2S standard gas was used for the quantitative repeatability test and, after 30-fold dynamic dilution, for determination of the sulfur detection limit. The quantitative repeatability, evaluated from the peak areas of seven consecutive injections, was 0.37%. The sulfur detection limit was 4.1 & times;10-13 g/s, and the linear range spanned approximately two orders of magnitude. The developed PFPD showed stable pulsed combustion behavior. It also provided reliable quantitative response for trace sulfur detection. The dual-EPC design helped clarify the relationship between ignition and analytical combustion. The optimized conditions provide an experimental basis for self-developed PFPD systems.

title: Methane Infrared Absorption Spectrum Denoising Filter Based on Hybrid Attention Autoencoder
authors: Lan, Xi; Lu, Yuting; Dong, Jiacheng; Jiang, Yicong; Du, Yuan; Guo, Ziyi; Zhu, Shouzheng; Wang, Senyuan; Li, Chunlai; Chen, Yuwei
abstract:
Objective Methane is both a critical greenhouse gas that significantly contributes to global climate change and a hazardous combustible gas with a low explosion threshold. Accurate and reliable detection of methane volume fraction is therefore of paramount importance for environmental governance, industrial safety, and public health protection. Among various sensing techniques, non-contact optical detection in open atmosphere based on active infrared absorption spectroscopy attracts increasing attention in industrial leak monitoring and atmospheric observation owing to its rapid temporal response, wide dynamic measurement range, and high molecular selectivity. However, in practical open-atmosphere measurement scenarios, spectral echo signals are inevitably contaminated by multiple noise sources, including detector noise, electronic noise, background radiation, and atmospheric scintillation noise induced by turbulence and refractive index fluctuations. These noise sources significantly degrade the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the acquired spectra and severely limit detection sensitivity. Although hardware-based optimization can partially suppress noise, it is often accompanied by increased system cost and complexity. As a result, advanced signal processing and denoising algorithms are cost-effective and indispensable methods for improving methane detection performance. Traditional spectral denoising methods rely heavily on predefined assumptions about noise statistics and spectral characteristics. As a consequence, they exhibit limited adaptability to complex and temporally varying noise environments and often lead to insufficient noise suppression or distortion of weak absorption features. Recently, supervised deep learning-based denoising methods demonstrate promising performance. However, these methods depend strongly on large-scale paired datasets consisting of noisy measurements and clean reference spectra. In practical outdoor measurements, truly clean reference spectra are generally unobtainable, which inevitably degrades model generalization and robustness. Unsupervised denoising frameworks attempt to reduce the dependence on clean references, but they are typically built upon the assumption of statistically independent noise realizations. This assumption is violated by atmospheric scintillation noise, which exhibits strong temporal correlation and structured fluctuations. Consequently, existing unsupervised methods struggle to effectively suppress such physically correlated noise. Therefore, the development of a robust, physically consistent, and unsupervised spectral denoising method tailored for non-contact methane detection in open atmosphere remains an urgent and challenging research problem. This study aims to address these problems by proposing a novel unsupervised deep learning-based denoising framework. Methods To overcome the aforementioned challenges, this paper proposes an unsupervised hybrid-attention convolutional autoencoder (HA-CAE) for methane spectral denoising. The proposed method is designed to suppress complex and temporally correlated noise while preserving weak absorption features, without relying on paired clean reference signals. The HA-CAE is constructed upon a convolutional autoencoder architecture, which encodes noisy spectral signals into a compact latent representation and subsequently reconstructs denoised spectra through a decoding process.

Unlike conventional autoencoders that rely solely on convolutional feature extraction, the proposed model integrates three complementary attention mechanisms to enhance feature learning capability from multiple perspectives. A global attention module is introduced to capture long-range dependencies and global correlations across the entire spectral sequence, enabling the network to distinguish structured signal components from distributed noise patterns. A local attention mechanism is employed to emphasize localized spectral features, allowing the model to preserve sharp absorption peaks and transient signal variations. In addition, a channel-wise attention module is incorporated to adaptively reweight spectral feature channels, highlighting informative bands associated with methane absorption while suppressing channels dominated by noise. The network is trained under an unsupervised learning paradigm using only noisy spectral measurements. Reconstruction loss is employed to encourage the network to learn noise-invariant representations by exploiting the intrinsic redundancy and structural consistency of spectral signals. This design eliminates the requirement for clean reference spectra and reduces the mismatch between algorithmic assumptions and real atmospheric noise characteristics. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, extensive experiments are conducted using low SNR methane spectral data acquired under laboratory conditions that emulate realistic standoff measurement environments in open atmosphere. The denoising performance of the proposed method is systematically compared with that of a conventional convolutional autoencoder and several classical filtering algorithms. Quantitative evaluation is performed using the SNR improvement metric, while qualitative analysis is carried out in both the temporal and spectral domains. Results and Discussions Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed HA-CAE significantly outperforms conventional denoising methods in both quantitative metrics and visual quality. The denoising results in the temporal domain show that the reconstructed spectral signals exhibit substantially reduced noise fluctuations while preserving the original absorption profiles. Compared with the noisy input signals, the denoised spectra show smoother baselines and clearer absorption features, indicating effective suppression of atmospheric scintillation noise and electronic noise. Comparative results in the temporal and spectral domains reveal that traditional filtering methods exhibit limited noise reduction capability and often introduce signal distortion or residual oscillations, particularly under low SNR conditions. The conventional autoencoder improves noise suppression to a certain extent but fails to adequately handle temporally correlated noise, leading to partial loss of fine spectral details. In contrast, the proposed method consistently achieves superior denoising performance across all evaluated scenarios. Quantitatively, the proposed method achieves an average SNR improvement of up to 63.19%, outperforming the conventional autoencoder by 11.65 percentage points and exceeding classical filtering methods by at least 27.42 percentage points. These results indicate that the hybrid attention mechanism plays a critical role in enhancing the network ability to discriminate between physically meaningful spectral information and complex noise components.

The improved performance in the spectral domain further confirms that the proposed method effectively suppresses broadband noise while preserving essential spectral energy distributions. Conclusions This paper presents an unsupervised HA-CAE for spectral denoising in non-contact methane detection under open-atmosphere conditions. By integrating global, local, and channel-wise attention mechanisms into a convolutional autoencoder framework, the proposed method effectively addresses the limitations of traditional filtering techniques and supervised deep learning-based methods. The proposed framework eliminates the dependence on clean reference spectra and overcomes the restrictive assumption of noise independence, making it well-suited for real atmospheric measurement environments dominated by temporally correlated scintillation noise. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves substantial SNR improvement and superior denoising performance in both temporal and spectral domains. The proposed method provides a robust and cost-effective signal processing solution for enhancing methane detection sensitivity and reliability. This work offers a promising pathway for the application of unsupervised deep learning techniques in optical gas sensing and contributes valuable insights for the future development of intelligent environmental monitoring systems.

title: Cascading effects of insufficient seed cold stratification across early life-stages in three temperate trees: impaired phenology and reduced seedling fitness under climate warming
abstract: Background and Aims Global warming is shortening winters in temperate ecosystems, limiting cold stratification for seeds with physiological dormancy (PD). The consequences of incomplete dormancy release can cascade beyond germination, potentially affecting fitness in subsequent life-stages, yet this remains understudied in trees. Here we assess the effects of insufficient stratification on germination, leaf emergence and seedling performance in three broad-range temperate tree species. We further evaluate how reduced cold stratification under climate change may drive shifts in these traits across the species distribution.Methods We sampled six Abies alba, six Acer pseudoplatanus and four Fagus sylvatica populations across their native distribution. 10 287 seeds of the three species were sown in climatic-controlled chambers at three different temperature regimes and two stratification treatments. We assessed the success, timing and synchrony of germination and first leaf emergence. We further monitored seedling growth and biomass, as well as root and leaf mass fractions. We analysed the effects of unfulfilled stratification in response to sowing temperature and the influence of populations' climate using generalized linear mixed effect models. We projected shifts in the studied traits under a SSP5-8.5 climate change scenario accounting for reduced cold stratification across the species native distributions.Key Results Missing cold stratification delayed germination time in all species and decreased F. sylvatica germination and leaf emergence proportions. It further constrained Ab. alba and F. sylvatica seedling growth, particularly under warm temperatures, irrespective of phenological changes. Spatial projections depicted important germination phenology changes across species distributions, uphill increases of Ab. alba seedling growth, and a decrease of F. sylvatica early fitness towards its western distribution.Conclusions Cold stratification improved seedling development and their performance under warming beyond regulating germination. Unfulfilled cold stratification in a warmer climate may therefore constrain temperate tree species seed regeneration even if germination proportions or phenology remain unaffected.

title: Performance evaluation of a modified cascaded m-w-shaped solar distiller integrated with staggered porous material and condensation basin
authors: Alghafis, Abdullah; Alrashidi, Abdullah; Alshammari, Fuhaid; Essa, Fadl A.
abstract: Freshwater scarcity represents a fundamental challenge to sustainable socio-economic development globally. Traditional basin-type conventional solar stills (CSS) offer an environmentally benign path to decentralized water security, but are typically constrained by low localized thermal efficiencies, limited evaporative surface areas, and suboptimal vapor condensation kinetics. To overcome these systemic thermodynamic constraints, this study introduces a cascaded auxiliary condensation-porous evaporation section to recover additional latent heat and enhance mass transfer. This paper presents a modified M-W-shaped solar still (MWSS) coupled with an advanced multi-stage auxiliary condensation layout. The innovative geometry incorporates a built-in W-shaped lower condensing glass profile that dual-functions as a multi-angled localized evaporating surface for an upper M-shaped condensing framework, establishing a synchronized cascaded thermal loop. To significantly amplify phase-change rates, the internal matrix incorporates five fabric-wick-wrapped vertical absorbers strategically arranged on the water section (three lower, two upper), thereby expanding the active evaporation area by 20 %. Furthermore, a fraction of concentrated basin brine is gravity-fed onto a staggered array of 21 fabric-wickcovered cylindrical porous pipes localized within a subjoined rectangular auxiliary condensation basin. Comprehensive comparative outdoor matrices reveal that the advanced modified M-W solar still (MMWSS) achieves a cumulative daily yield of 6.64 L/m2 & sdot;day, representing a substantial 120.6 % increase over the baseline CSS (3.01 L/m2 & sdot;day). MMWSS with internal vertical absorbers and the integrated auxiliary porous-material condensation basin) achieves a daily freshwater productivity of 7.68 L/m2 & sdot;day with a total distillate enhancement of 155.15 %. Thermodynamic evaluations indicate that the maximum daily thermal and exergy efficiencies for the advanced MMWSS with porous basin are 58.4 % and 5.36 %, respectively, compared with 31.2 % and 1.85 % for the CSS.
