Economic analyses indicate a significantly reduced cost per liter (CPL) of $0.01/L and a shorter capital payback period, while environmental life-cycle metrics demonstrate a lifetime carbon mitigation potential exceeding 42.1 tons of CO2 equivalent, validating the high viability of the proposed architecture for sustainable decentralized desalination.

title: Evaluation of gasification agent strategies for underground coal gasification in post-ECBM reservoirs: A coupled thermo-hydro-chemical numerical simulation approach
authors: Hu, Zhuocheng; Yao, Jun; Sun, Hai; Wang, Zijie; Li, Jinlong; Li, Longlong; An, Guoqiang; Zhao, Dali; Zhang, Lei; Sang, Qian; Yang, Yongfei; Huang, Zhaoqin; Grasselli, Giovanni
abstract: Implementing underground coal gasification (UCG) in post-ECBM reservoirs, namely coal reservoirs after CO2enhanced coalbed methane (CO2-ECBM) recovery, provides a potential pathway for residual energy recovery. However, the pre-existing CO2-rich environment alters reservoir conditions and introduces additional constraints on gasification agent selection and process control. In this study, an in-house coupled thermo-hydro-chemical (THC) simulator was developed to investigate UCG under CO2-rich post-ECBM reservoir conditions. The gasification performance of different gasification agent strategies, including pure O2 injection, CO2-O2 co-injection, and water coinjection with O2, was systematically evaluated under various injection rates, together with a simplified screeninglevel cost assessment based on the assumed cost parameters. The results demonstrate that UCG can be initiated and maintained under the investigated reservoir, operating, and kinetic conditions. During gasification, the CO2 distribution evolves dynamically with cavity development, suggesting its potential to reflect reaction-zone evolution. For pure oxygen injection, increasing the injection rate accelerates coal conversion and reduces unit gas cost, but decreases syngas lower heating value and combustible component fraction. Compared with pure oxygen injection, CO2-O2 coinjection increases residual coal mass and results in lower syngas quality and higher unit gas cost under the investigated conditions. In contrast, moderate water co-injection improves syngas quality and reduces unit energy cost at low-to-moderate oxygen injection rates by promoting steam-related gasification reactions. Among the simulated cases, an oxygen injection rate of 3 & times; 10-4 m3/s combined with a water injection rate of 3 & times; 10-6 m3/s exhibited the most favorable overall performance within the investigated parameter range. Overall, this study provides insights into the thermochemical response of UCG under post-ECBM conditions and offers a numerical basis for comparative evaluation of gasification strategies prior to experimental and engineering-scale investigations.

title: Ten questions concerning air movement as a primary cooling strategy: "Fan-first" cooling
authors: Tartarini, Federico; Chong, Adrian; Cheung, Toby; Jay, Ollie; Kent, Michael G.; Li, Jiayu; Lipczynska, Aleksandra; Mahdavi, Ardeshir; Pasut, Wilmer; Popiolek, Zbigniew; Raftery, Paul; Ravanelli, Nicholas; Taber, Christian; Tham, Kwok Wai; Wilkins, Arnold J.; Schiavon, Stefano
abstract: Conventional cooling assumes that indoor air must be both cooled and kept still. While effective for maintaining thermal comfort and protecting occupants from heat stress, this approach is highly energy-intensive and costly. Raising air speed while allowing a higher air temperature can produce the same cooling sensation as still air at a lower temperature, with all other environmental and personal factors held constant, at only a fraction of the energy demand. Here, we argue for a "fan-first" approach that prioritises air movement as the primary cooling mechanism, applying mechanical cooling only when necessary, across mechanically conditioned, mixed-mode, and naturally ventilated buildings. We propose ten questions addressing the benefits and challenges of this approach across thermal comfort, energy efficiency, visual comfort, and indoor air quality, synthesising current evidence and identifying critical gaps for future research. Across these questions, evidence indicates that "fan-first" strategies can maintain thermal comfort at indoor temperatures of 27-30 degrees C, deliver cooling-energy savings of 20-40 %, and reduce zone-level Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) construction costs by up to 35 %, while also supporting indoor air quality through improved room-scale mixing. While ceiling fans receive the most attention given the breadth of available ev idence, the underlying principles apply to any device that elevates air speed across the body, including desk, pedestal, and portable fans. Aimed at researchers, practitioners, and policymakers, this article encourages broader adoption of air movement as a viable, sustainable cooling strategy, reducing reliance on energy-intensive mechanical systems.

title: A high-performance Si0.5Ge0.5 source vertical nanowire TFET for ultra-sensitive biosensing and high-speed comparator applications
authors: Bhardwaj, Anjana; Kumar, Abhishek; Swarnima; Sharma, Upasana
abstract: In this work, a SixGe1-x source-engineered vertical nanowire tunnel field effect transistor (VNW-TFET) is proposed and systematically investigated for biosensing and circuit applications. The effect of Ge mole fraction (x = 0-0.9) is analyzed, and it is observed that the Si0.5Ge0.5 configuration exhibits optimal performance, providing a balanced trade-off between enhanced band-to-band tunneling and controlled leakage current. Based on this optimized structure, a dielectrically modulated biosensor is designed, and its performance is evaluated for different dielectric constants (k = 2.1-12). The results show that the device sensitivity increases significantly with k due to enhanced electric field and tunneling probability, achieving a maximum I-ON sensitivity of 2036 and I-ON/I-OFF sensitivity of 1.6 & times; 10(6). Further, device optimization is performed by varying key parameters such as cavity thickness (2-2.4 nm), cavity length (24-36 nm), temperature (200-400 K), and drain voltage (0.4-1.4 V). It is observed that reduced cavity thickness enhances performance, while cavity length has minimal impact, confirming that sensing is dominated by the tunneling region. The device also exhibits stable operation under temperature variations. To validate circuit-level applicability, the proposed device is modeled in Verilog-A and implemented in Cadence to design a comparator circuit. The comparator achieves a slew rate of 5 MV mu s(-1), propagation delay of 242 ps, dynamic power of 112 mW, and static power of 28.6 mu W. The proposed Si0.5Ge0.5-VNW-TFET demonstrates excellent performance in terms of sensitivity, speed, and power efficiency, making it a promising candidate for next-generation biosensing and low-power circuit applications.

title: Cinnamaldehyde-lactic acid deep eutectic solvent modified chitosan composite film and its application in grape preservation
authors: Xu, Wanqin; Liu, Qun; Zeng, Xu; Sun, Xiaobo; Weng, Wuyin; Zhang, Yucang
abstract: To address the issues of non-degradability in traditional petroleum-based packaging materials and the limitations of chitosan (CS) films (e.g., poor mechanical properties, insufficient water resistance, and single functionality), this study incorporated a deep eutectic solvent (DES) composed of cinnamaldehyde (CIN) and DL-lactic acid (LA) into the CS matrix to fabricate high-performance composite films. The effect of DES content on the structure and properties of the composite films was investigated. FTIR and XPS analyses suggested that a fraction of the aldehyde groups of CIN participated in Schiff base formation with the amino groups of CS. Together with hydrogen-bond reorganization and LA induced protonation of CS amino groups, these interactions contributed to the regulation of the CS network. When the DES content was 60% of the dry weight of CS, the resulting CS(CIN: LA)60 film exhibited the optimal comprehensive performance: its tensile strength (TS) reached as high as 41.57 MPa; the water contact angle (WCA) was approximately 100 degrees, indicating good hydrophobicity; the water vapor transmission rate (WVTR) was reduced to 560.2 g/(m2 & sdot;24h); meanwhile, it possessed excellent ultraviolet (UV) shielding ability, remarkable anti-fogging performance, and good antibacterial activity. Grape preservation experiments demonstrated that the CS(CIN:LA)60 film could effectively inhibit microbial growth, reduce water loss, and delay fruit softening and the degradation of nutritional components. Compared with commercial polyethylene (PE) cling film, the composite film showed advantages in antibacterial activity, anti-fogging performance, and the maintenance of several grape quality attributes. This study provides a new strategy for the development of green food packaging materials.

title: Multifunctional gel beads derived from coal gangue-phosphorus tailings layered double hydroxides for Cd(II) immobilization
authors: Zhao, Pei; Ye, Qinhan; Xia, Xuan; Xiao, Yang; Xin, Bingran; Li, Dou; Chen, Jinyi; Qiu, Xinhong
abstract: Remediating heavy metal-polluted soils requires not only effective contaminant immobilization but also water conservation and fertility restoration. In this study, polyacrylamide-layered double hydroxide gel beads (hereafter referred to as RFW-LDH beads, where RFW denotes Cd(II) remediation, fertilizer release, and water retention) were synthesized using solid wastes derived from coal gangue and phosphorus tailings. Their multifunctional performance, including Cd(II) immobilization, water retention, controlled fertilizer release, and magnetic recovery, was systematically evaluated. RFW-LDH beads exhibited excellent Cd(II) immobilization, primarily attributed to the synergistic contributions of polymer matrix complexation/coordination, LDH surface adsorption, and isomorphic substitution. Their stability was confirmed through the toxicity characteristic leaching procedure (TCLP), dry-wet cycling, and freeze-thaw tests. Sequential extraction further demonstrated the transformation of Cd into more stable fractions following remediation. Urea release from the beads was independent of environmental conditions and followed a two-stage pattern: an initial rapid release driven by surface swelling, followed by a slower diffusion-controlled phase. Swelling-deswelling and soil water-holding experiments showed that the beads effectively delayed evaporation and improved soil moisture retention. Plant toxicity assays revealed reduced Cd accumulation and mitigated phytotoxicity, while tissue carbon and nitrogen analyses confirmed enhanced soil fertility resulting from the encapsulated urea. Microbial community shifts indicated improved carbon and nitrogen cycling and overall enhancement of soil properties. Additionally, the incorporation of magnetic Fe3O4 imparted strong magnetic responsiveness, enabling rapid and nondestructive recovery under an external magnetic field. Collectively, the RFW-LDH beads integrate heavy metal immobilization, water retention, nutrient supply, and magnetic recovery into a single platform, offering a green, efficient, and sustainable strategy for remediating polluted soils.

title: Multiscale insights into the microstructure and mechanical behavior of Ag-doped Zr-based amorphous microwires
authors: Zhang, Peng; Liu, Jingshun; Yu, Shiyang; Ma, Yunfei; Ma, Shuang
abstract: The effects of Ag-doping on the microstructure, thermal stability, and mechanical behavior of Zr53.5Cu29.5xNi5Al12Agx (x = 0-7 at.%) amorphous microwires (AMWs) were systematically investigated through experimental characterization combined with multiscale simulations. The results demonstrate that appropriate Agdoping significantly enhances the thermal stability and mechanical properties of Zr-based AMWs, with the Zr53.5Cu27.5Ni5Al12Ag2 (Ag2) AMW exhibiting a larger supercooled liquid region of 53.5 K, higher enthalpy change of 55.81 J/g, ultimate tensile strength of 2630 MPa, hardness of 6.3 GPa, and elastic modulus of 104.4 GPa ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations reveal that 2 at.% Ag-doping reduces atomic-scale structural heterogeneity through enhanced atomic packing efficiency, increased fractions of icosahedral-like local structures, strengthened Zr-Ni and Cu-Al atomic correlations, and enlarged medium-range order size. These atomic-scale features enhance structural stability, thereby contributing to the improved thermal stability of the Ag2 AMW. Furthermore, classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide atomistic insights into the deformation mechanisms during tensile loading, demonstrating that the Ag2 AMW maintains dispersed shear transformation zone (STZ) activation and homogeneous shear deformation at high strains, which is consistent with a reduced tendency for shear localization and a delayed development of dominant shear bands. In contrast, excessive Ag-doping is associated with STZ aggregation and promotes shear localization. These findings provide multiscale insights into the relationship between structural characteristics and macroscopic mechanical behavior, offering guidance for the design of high-performance Zr-based AMWs.

title: Reduction of nanoparticle formation by humid air in single iron microparticle combustion
authors: Elsasser, Leon; Bonarens, Matthias; Li, Yuhang; Dreizler, Andreas; Li, Tao
abstract: Iron is a promising recyclable energy carrier in the metal fuel cycle; however, nanoparticle (NP) formation during combustion reduces fuel efficiency and raises emission concerns. While elevated particle temperatures are known to promote iron evaporation and NP formation, the role of ambient humidity in particle-tonanoparticle conversion remains unresolved. Here, single iron microparticles (51.5 +/- 3.2 mu m) were combusted in a drop-tube reactor under dry and humid atmospheres at nominal 20% and 40% O-2. Time-resolved dual-wavelength pyrometry and diffuse backlight illumination (DBI) at 10 kHz simultaneously resolved particle surface temperature, luminosity, diameter evolution, and NP cloud intensity from microparticle melting through NP formation to NP cloud detachment. Water mole fraction was quantified in situ using tunable diode laser absorption spectroscopy. Humid conditions with chi(H2O) approximate to 14-15% (v) reduce the apparent peak particle temperature by 6%-8%, causing an exponential decrease in iron vapor pressure and evaporative mass flux. As a result, NP onset is delayed, formation duration shortens (at nominal 20% O-2), and peak NP cloud intensity decreases by more than 80% compared to dry conditions. The suppressing effect of humidity exceeds the enhancement induced by increased oxygen concentration. Mechanistically, reduced vapor pressure and delayed transition to outward nanoparticle transport lower supersaturation and nucleation rates, thereby diminishing NP formation. These findings show that humidity fundamentally alters microparticle-to-nanoparticle conversion in iron combustion and provide quantitative benchmarks for predictive modeling and emission control in metal-fueled systems. Novelty and significance statement: This work presents the first quantitative, time-resolved investigation of humidity effects on nanoparticle formation during single iron microparticle combustion. Previous in situ studies correlated particle temperature with nanoparticle (NP) onset, primarily addressing effects of particle size and oxygen levels rather than humidity . Other investigations tracked NP cloud evolution without simultaneous quantitative surface-temperature measurements , while studies of humid iron flames did not isolate single-particle behavior. By combining full NP cloud tracking with simultaneous dual-wavelength surface-temperature measurements under controlled dry and humid atmospheres, this study enables a mechanistic assessment of how water vapor modifies evaporation, supersaturation, and microparticle-to-nanoparticle conversion. In addition, this work developed a novel optical setup for two-color pyrometry system using a single camera with an image doubler.

title: Phase transition analysis of mixed traffic string stability: Closed-form critical penetration rate and topology effects
authors: Wang, Xinrui; Yang, Panpan; Liu, Zhaolun
venue: PHYSICA A-STATISTICAL MECHANICS AND ITS APPLICATIONS
abstract: The incremental deployment of connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) is producing a decades-long coexistence with human-driven vehicles (HDVs), while the minimum CAV fraction needed to stabilize this mixed traffic remains unknown, with reported thresholds ranging from a few percent to nearly half. This spread precludes a transferable deployment target, while the phase transition character and topology dependence of the stability boundary remain unclear. This paper removes the combinatorial barrier by recasting the multiplicative head-to-tail stability condition as an additive Lyapunov exponent. The criterion reduces to a scalar function of the HDV and CAV frequency responses. For a single-lane stream under linearized car-following dynamics, this yields a closed-form critical penetration rate. The resulting threshold is therefore a lower bound that excludes lane changing, communication delay, and actuator saturation. Within this scope, the stability transition exhibits mean-field finite-size scaling, with data collapse confirmed across platoon sizes from 50 to 1000 vehicles. In the large-system limit, random and structured deployments share the same threshold, so stability depends on the CAV fraction alone. Simulations confirm these analytical predictions within 1% and show robustness under nonlinear perturbations. The threshold also depends on information flow topology: under topology-appropriate gains, Multi-Successor Leading reduces the required CAV proportion by 70% relative to Predecessor Following. Application to 649 naturalistic trajectories from the HighD dataset reproduces the full range of reported thresholds as a monotonic function of CAV control aggressiveness.

title: Transferability of foundation MACE models to amorphous chemistry: Where they work and where they fail
authors: Malyi, Oleksandr I.; Usuga, Andres Felipe
abstract: Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials have the potential to achieve first-principles-like accuracy at a significantly reduced computational cost, and have become one of the main breakthroughs in computational materials science. However, their transferability to new materials chemistry remains unclear. Motivated by this, herein, we benchmark 27 parameterizations derived from 16 foundation multi-atomic cluster expansion (MACE) pretrained models against density functional theory (DFT) energies for a set of 23 amorphous compounds generated by melt-quench molecular dynamics. We show that MACE generally preserves the ordering of structures but often distorts the energetic scale. Specifically, across 621 model-compound pairs, similar to 77% of fitted relative-energy slopes are below 1. In practical terms, these results suggest that a large fraction of MACE potentials are unable to predict the DFT distribution of local motifs in amorphous solids due to the underestimation of the energy difference between low and high-energy structural motifs abundant in amorphous solids. Among the tested models, MH-1/OMAT-PBE performs best overall with a weighted relative mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.02 eV/atom, followed by MH-0/OMAT-PBE and OMAT-0-M. However, the obtained results are highly chemistry-dependent. Specifically, amorphous oxides are described much more robustly than elemental networks, with weighted relative mean absolute errors of 0.02 and 0.09 eV/atom, respectively. The existence of the best overall model does not imply that the model is best for every compound, and hence, chemistry-aware model selection is essential for reliable amorphous-phase simulations.

title: Assessing the effectiveness of barrier allocation strategies against the propagation of phytopathogens and pests with percolation
authors: Garcia Prieto, E. G.; Garcia Morales, G.; Silva Montiel, J. D.; Rosales Herrera, D.; Alvarado Garcia, J. R.; Fernandez Tellez, A.; Martinez Laguna, Y.; Lopez-Olguin, J. F.; Ramirez, J. E.
abstract: We investigate the connectivity properties of square lattices with nearest neighbor interactions, where some sites have a reduced coordination number, meaning that certain sites can only connect through three or two adjacent sites. This model is similar to the random placement of physical barriers in plantations aimed at decreasing connectivity between susceptible individuals, which could help prevent the spread of phytopathogens and pests. In this way, we estimate the percolation threshold as a function of p(d) (the fraction of sites with reduced coordination number), finding that a q-exponential function can well describe the critical curves. Additionally, we derive a closed formula for the correlation between p(d) and the density of distinct barriers placed (accounting for shared barriers between adjacent sites). The latter is helpful in estimating the relative costs of the barrier allocation strategies. In particular, we found that the allocations of two barriers per site model{(sic) ,(sic)} can produce savings between 5% and 10% of the strategy cost compared to the independently random barrier allocations (joint site-bond percolation). From an agroecology perspective, adding barriers to the plantation gives farmers the opportunity to sow more vulnerable plant varieties.

title: A SNP panel for coanalysis of capture and shotgun ancient DNA data
authors: Fournier, Romain; Pearson Fulton, Alice; Tabin, Daniel; Reich, David
abstract: Advances in technology have decreased the cost of generating genetic data from ancient people, resulting in exponentially increasing numbers of individuals with whole-genome data. However, these technologies come with platform-specific biases, limiting coanalyzability of individuals sequenced with different technologies as well as joint analysis of modern and ancient individuals. Here, we present a method to identify single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) with minimal technology-specific bias. Leveraging data from more than 18,000 individuals, we apply this method to identify a set of around 1 million SNPs that we call the "compatibility" panel, which has been effectively assayed in a large fraction of ancient human DNA experiments published to date. We also identify a subset of these SNPs, the "compatibility-HO" panel, which are restricted to positions that have been assayed in more than 10,000 modern people from more than 1000 diverse populations using the Affymetrix Human Origins (HO) genotyping array. The compatibility panel reduces spurious Z-scores owing to differing sequencing platforms by nearly an order of magnitude, while retaining similar to 60%-85% of statistical power for f-statistic analysis. We also provide a tool for users to select different tradeoffs between bias and power as well as sequencing platforms for their specific analyses.

title: Membraneless flow-through water electrolysis: The importance of cell geometry
authors: Postma, J. i.; Yahyaee, A.; Haverkort, J. w.
abstract: Membraneless flow-through water electrolysers keep the generated hydrogen away from oxygen bubbles by forced convection, removing membrane costs while improving energy efficiency. Previously, micrometre holes were used to ensure a homogeneous flow distribution. Here, we strongly reduce flow resistance using electrodes with large holes, while a discharge channel that widens in the direction of the main flow improves flow distribution. At too low liquid velocities, we provide direct in-situ measurements showing that the bubble size between the electrodes increases over time and with height due to coalescence. Counterintuitively, we find that a straight discharge channel requires less liquid flow. Using a combination of multiphase simulations and imaging experiments, we find that the higher velocity through the final downstream holes in a straight discharge channel prevents gas bubbles in the gap. The superficial velocity at which the electrolyte enters the feed channel must be an order of magnitude greater than that of the hydrogen produced at the electrode. The electrolyte velocity through the last holes should be even two orders of magnitude greater, so the gas fraction stays well below 1 percent there. Interestingly, at lower liquid flow rates, computational fluid dynamics predicts that natural electrolyte convection diverts the flow towards the hydrogen-producing electrode. By identifying the local flow requirements, this work helps to balance low pressure drop with effective gas bubble removal in membraneless electrolysers.

title: A cost-effective enzymatic strategy for high-efficiency aril removal and quality preservation in Torreya grandis nuts during the postripening stage
authors: Gao, Yadi; Chen, Shanshan; Fang, Di'er; Wei, Xixing; Chu, Tiansheng; Farag, Mohamed A.; Diao, Songfeng; Yu, Weiwu; Song, Lili; Gan, Yi; Hu, Yuanyuan
abstract: Torreya grandis is an economic nut tree endemic to southern China. Aril removal is necessary for the post-ripening and processing of its nuts. However, due to the high cost of batch harvesting, production often involves harvesting large quantities of uncracked nuts, making aril removal time-consuming and labor-intensive, and often causing serious damage. In this study, we systematically optimized the enzymatic peeling process through three sequential steps: screening for effective pre-treatments to overcome the waxy cuticle barrier, conducting singlefactor experiments coupled with Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to identify optimal conditions, and performing comparative evaluation of two enzymatic peeling processes (knife cutting plus enzymatic peeling, namely KCE; and chemical dewaxing plus enzymatic peeling, namely DWE). The results showed that physical incisions made by knife cutting and a composite chemical dewaxing agent consisting of 600 mL/L ethanol and 50 g/L sucrose fatty acid ester, effectively overcame the waxy barrier. The optimal conditions were identified as follows: pH 4.0, 34 degrees C, 274 mL/L enzyme concentration and a volume proportion of 3.5:3:1 (Vpectinase: Vcellulase: Vhemicellulase). Additionally, both KCE and DWE significantly increased water-soluble pectin and degraded cellulose, facilitating efficient peeling while markedly reducing off-flavor volatiles (terpinen-4-ol and 2-octanone). Compared to DWE, KCE offered shorter processing time (30 vs. 50 min) and longer enzyme longevity (8 vs. 4 cycles). This technology enhances peeling efficiency and product quality, providing a sustainable and effective strategy for T. grandis nuts, which may also be applicable to other nut species.

title: Nitrogen-Driven Microbial Functional Rewiring Dictates Soil Carbon Dynamics in High-Altitude Apple Orchards: A Metagenomic Perspective
authors: Huang, Wenqiang; Wu, Zheng; Tong, Lingchen; Hu, Minghang; Liu, Shuang; Han, Yanying; Zhang, Guangyu; Ye, Yanhui
venue: JOURNAL OF SOIL SCIENCE AND PLANT NUTRITION
abstract: Understanding the impacts of nitrogen (N) fertilization on soil carbon (C) and N cycling, and the underlying micro-ecological mechanisms, is critical for alpine agroecosystems. This study investigates these non-linear dynamics to address the knowledge gap in high-altitude perennial orchard systems. We conducted a continuous six-year N addition gradient experiment (initiated in 2019) with four rates (0, 150, 300, and 450 kg ha(-)& sup1; yr(-)& sup1;) in a Xizang alpine apple orchard. Our methodology integrated metagenomic binning to reconstruct metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), extracellular enzyme assays, and soil organic carbon (SOC) physical and biochemical fractionation. SOC accumulation followed a non-linear trajectory, peaking under the 300 kg ha(-)& sup1; yr(-)& sup1; (N300) treatment with a 39.3% increase relative to the unfertilized control. Genome-resolved analysis revealed that N300 synergistically enhanced cellobiohydrolase and beta-1,4-N-acetylglucosaminidase activities. This coincided with higher relative abundances of multifunctional coupled microbial taxa (e.g., Pyrinomonadales), and was accompanied by the highest fungal necromass carbon and a 38.21% increase in particulate organic carbon (POC). Conversely, the 450 kg ha(-)& sup1; yr(-)& sup1; (N450) treatment induced severe soil acidification and significantly inhibited polyphenol oxidase activity by 30.56%. This triggered C-N functional decoupling as the microbial community shifted toward N-degradation-dominated taxa like Rhodanobacter spp. Although N450 reduced active C proportions, it was accompanied by a 46.69% increase in MAOC, consistent with a potential contribution of bacterial necromass to mineral-associated C formation. Soil C pool differentiation is governed by a cascading pathway spanning from environmental filtering through functional rewiring. Within the tested N gradient, the N300 treatment provided the most favorable balance between SOC accumulation, microbial functional coordination, and labile C maintenance in this alpine orchard system. Furthermore, excessive N application poses a clear trade-off, where enhanced MAOC sequestration comes at the cost of severe soil acidification and a substantial decline in active carbon pools.

title: Thermal energy storage performance of encapsulated palm waste derived bio based phase change materials for solar cooling applications
abstract: The increasing cooling demand and high electricity consumption of conventional air-conditioning systems have intensified interest in sustainable thermal energy storage solutions. This study presents a comprehensive review of solar cooling systems integrated with encapsulated palm waste derived bio based phase change materials for building applications. Particular emphasis is placed on thermal energy storage performance, including latent heat storage capacity, charging discharging behavior, thermal regulation, and load-shifting capability under tropical climatic conditions. The study evaluates the integration of bio-based phase change materials in absorption, adsorption, desiccant, and photovoltaic (PV) driven cooling systems while examining techno-economic and environmental performance. Palm-based materials with phase transition temperatures of 20-30 degrees C and latent heat capacities of 150-220 kJ kg(-1) demonstrate strong suitability for cooling-oriented thermal energy storage. Storage integration improves cooling continuity, enhances solar utilization, and reduces peak thermal loads, achieving energy savings of 20-40% and solar fractions of 60-70%. Economic analysis indicates that palmbased materials provide lower cost compared with conventional paraffin-based storage materials, with payback periods of 3-8 years despite encapsulation expenses. Environmental assessment further demonstrates significant carbon emission reduction potential. Encapsulated palm waste derived materials represent a promising low carbon thermal energy storage solution for sustainable solar cooling applications.

title: Representative virtual heliostat: A reduced-order approach to accelerate flux estimation for a central receiver tower system
authors: Yadav, Aditya; Raj, Manish; Bhattacharya, Jishnu
abstract: Flux estimation over the receiver surface is critical in design and analysis of a concentrating solar power (CSP) system based on heliostat field and central receiver tower. Monte Carlo ray tracing (MCRT) provides high accuracy in estimating flux distribution. However, it is computationally too expensive to be employed for yearround estimation for various sun-positions, or for different receiver geometries, for a large heliostat field of practical use. To address this limitation, a novel method is developed in the current study where a reduced-order framework based on Representative Virtual Heliostats (RVH) is introduced. In the present approach, particle swarm optimization (PSO) is employed to identify one or more RVHs which reproduce the optical signature of the full heliostat field on the receiver-vertical plane via utilization of only a fraction of the computational resource. Optimization minimises the deviation between the flux distribution generated by the RVHs and that obtained from the full-field MCRT. For a heliostat field of small width, a single RVH suffices. On the other hand, for large heliostat fields, multiple RVHs are introduced to preserve directional variation in the incident flux distribution. A scaling strategy is implemented to maintain parity in the input energy between the full-field MCRT and the RVH ray tracing. The proposed methodology is tested against the full-field MCRT across multiple sun positions spread through a year. It is demonstrated that the RVH-based novel method can effectively expedite feasibility estimation for the flux distribution on the receiver vertical plane with minimal loss of accuracy.

title: Electrode Architecture Effects on Lithium-Ion Battery Aging: A Pseudo-Two-Dimensional Modeling Approach
authors: Giusti, Irene; De Santis, Marella; Poli, Federico; Piancastelli, Luca; Liverani, Alfredo
venue: JOURNAL OF ELECTROCHEMICAL ENERGY CONVERSION AND STORAGE
abstract: This study investigates the electrochemical performance and aging behavior of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), focusing on the architectural effects of electrode and separator geometries alongside active material particle sizes. A pseudo-two-dimensional (P2D) model is employed to simulate lithium intercalation, solid diffusion, and coupled thermal behavior across a full-factorial design space. Despite its one-dimensional formulation, the model provides an optimal balance between computational efficiency and comparative predictive capability. A range of cell configurations is analyzed by varying anode, cathode, and separator thicknesses, as well as particle sizes, to assess their coupled impact on cell performance. The results demonstrate that while smaller particle diameters mitigate solid-state diffusion limitations and enhance capacity retention specifically under high C-rates, minimizing separator thickness significantly reduces inactive mass fractions, boosting baseline specific capacity even in designs with larger commercial particles. However, higher electrode loadings lead to increased volumetric heat-generation rates, particularly within thicker electrode configurations. A comparative assessment is also conducted in terms of cell mass, enabling the estimation of specific energy and power scaled to a standard format. Although limited to relative heat-generation trends by the one-dimensional thermal approximation, the results provide practical guidelines for advanced LIB design, successfully balancing electrochemical performance, volumetric engineering, and computational cost.

title: Variational Stokes method applied to free surface boundaries in numerical geodynamical models using the staggered-grid finite-difference discretisation
authors: Gray, Timothy S.; Tackley, Paul J.; Gerya, Taras V.
abstract: Accurately and efficiently modelling topographic evolution is a key challenge in geodynamic modelling, which requires the solution of the Stokes equations with free surface boundary conditions. While finite difference methods on staggered grids, as used in geodynamic modelling codes such as StagYY, I3ELVIS and LaMEM, offer strong computational performance and compatibility with multigrid solvers, the use of fixed Eulerian grids complicates the implementation of realistic, deformable free surfaces. Two existing methods are available to model free surface boundary conditions in such codes: the commonly used sticky-air method, which suffers from limitations relating to high viscosity contrasts, and the "staircase" method, which improves upon the sticky air method by imposing free surface boundary conditions at cell boundaries.To address the limitations of existing methods of implementing free surface boundary conditions, this study investigates an alternative variational discretisation of the Stokes equations that uses volume fractions to represent a smooth surface within a fixed Eulerian grid, allowing the imposition of accurate free surface boundary conditions while allowing it to bypass the limitations of existing free surface discretisation methods.The variational Stokes method is demonstrated to be an accurate and computationally efficient alternative to existing methods. It reproduces results comparable to existing methods while reducing computational cost and enabling broader applications, including non-zero surface tractions, complex surface loading, and compatibility with 3D spherical geometries.

title: Early Versus Delayed Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients With NSTEMI and Stable Heart Failure
authors: Hanif, Muhammad; Bhat, Vivek; Mufarreh, Anthony; Chaudhuri, Debanik; Kalra, Ankur
abstract: Background Early percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has been shown to improve outcomes in certain high-risk patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), but its optimal timing in those with stable heart failure (HF) remains unclear. Aim We aimed to compared 1 month and 1 year cardiovascular outcomes between early (< 24 h) and delayed (>= 24 h) PCI in patients with NSTEMI with stable HF. Methods We identified adults with both NSTEMI and HF in TriNetX, then divided them based on PCI timing. We excluded patients with decompensated HF, STEMI, or pregnancy. Cohorts were then balanced using propensity-score matching, with standardized mean difference < 0.1. Our primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, HF exacerbation, recurrent myocardial infarction (MI), and ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation (VT/VF). Secondary outcomes included individual primary outcome components, acute kidney injury, and major bleeding. Outcomes were assessed at 1 month and 1 year, expressed as relative risks (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Results After matching, we included 2249 patients in each cohort. After PSM, the mean age of the early PCI cohort was 69.3 +/- 11.5 years, while that of the delayed PCI cohort was 69.2 +/- 11.7 years, with 35% women. Hypertension (84.8%), hyperlipidemia (67.2%), and diabetes mellitus (53.1%) were the most prevalent comorbidities. Patients included both HF with preserved and reduced ejection fraction (HFpEF and HFrEF). Early PCI was associated with a higher risk of the primary outcome at both 1 month (RR = 1.23, 95% CI: 1.15-1.31, p < 0.01) and 1 year (RR = 1.12, 95% CI: 1.07-1.18, p < 0.01), compared with delayed PCI. Early PCI was associated with higher risk of recurrent MI at both time points, while risk of all-cause mortality and VT/VF were similar. Risk of HF exacerbation was higher with early PCI at 1 month but was comparable at 1 year. Conclusion In patients with NSTEMI and stable HF, early PCI was associated with higher risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes, warranting further investigation in this understudied subgroup.

title: Floxels: Fast Unsupervised Voxel Based Scene Flow Estimation
authors: Hoffmann, David T.; Raza, Syed Haseeb; Jiang, Hanqiu; Tananaev, Denis; Klingenhoefer, Steffen; Meinke, Martin
venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF CONFERENCE ON COMPUTER VISION AND PATTERN RECOGNITION (CVPR)
abstract: Scene flow estimation is a foundational task for many robotic applications, including robust dynamic object detection, automatic labeling, and sensor synchronization. Two types of approaches to the problem have evolved: 1) Supervised and 2) optimization-based methods. Supervised methods are fast during inference and achieve high-quality results, however, they are limited by the need for large amounts of labeled training data and are susceptible to domain gaps. In contrast, unsupervised test-time optimization methods do not face the problem of domain gaps but usually suffer from substantial runtime, exhibit artifacts, or fail to converge to the right solution. In this work, we mitigate several limitations of existing optimization-based methods. To this end, we 1) introduce a simple voxel grid-based model that improves over the standard MLP-based formulation in multiple dimensions and 2) introduce a new multi-frame loss formulation. 3) We combine both contributions in our new method, termed Floxels. On the Argoverse 2 benchmark, Floxels is surpassed only by EulerFlow among unsupervised methods while achieving comparable performance at a fraction of the computational cost. Floxels achieves a massive speedup of more than similar to 60 - 140x over EulerFlow, reducing the runtime from a day to 10 minutes per sequence. Over the faster but low-quality baseline, NSFP, Floxels achieves a speedup of similar to 14x.

title: Age-dependent properties of fine fractions from landfill mining: implications for resource recovery
authors: Chen, Ping; Yang, Yijian; Bian, Yi; Qiu, Yufeng; Zheng, Kangqi; Guo, Qi-Meng; Zhan, Liang-Tong; Yang, Dong; Li, Shuisheng
venue: JOURNAL OF MATERIAL CYCLES AND WASTE MANAGEMENT
abstract: The sustainable utilization of fine fractions from landfill mining remains a key challenge in waste management. This study examines geotechnical and environmental characteristics of soil-like fine fractions (< 15 mm) from the Woqishan landfill, China, with an apparent age range of 23-37 years. Observed age-dependent trends reflect combined biochemical degradation and physical processes. With increasing storage period and depth, organic content, particle size (D60), hydraulic conductivity (0.247 to 0.183 mm/s), and internal friction angle decreased, while specific gravity, water-holding capacity (375.1 to 502.2 g/kg), and cohesion increased. D60 and hydraulic conductivity are the most influential parameters governing engineering performance. The fine fractions have a sandy loam texture and abundant nutrients (N, P, K), but heavy metal concentrations exceed safety standards for direct agricultural use. Particles < 2 mm account for 50% of the mass yet contain > 90% of total heavy metals (Cu, Zn, Cd, Ni, Pb). We therefore recommend screening at 2 mm as pretreatment. The coarse fraction (2-15 mm) is relatively clean and suitable for direct engineering use, while the fine fraction (< 2 mm) is treated and then reused for non-food applications or recombined with the coarse fraction. This approach reduces pretreatment costs and enhance efficiency in large-scale resource utilization. Highlights Studied wastes storage period reached 37 years, 15 years beyond literature records. Strong correlations were observed between geotechnical properties and storage period. Heavy metals tend to accumulate in the fine fractions with a particle size <2 mm.

title: Effects of austenitizing time on microstructure and hydrogen environment-assisted cracking behavior of M54 steel
authors: Dong, Lijin; Dong, Caiyun; Liu, Jiuyun; Liao, Yunbo; Zheng, Huaibei; Liu, Tingyao; Wang, Qinying
abstract: Ferrium M54 steel offers a cost-effective alternative to AerMet 100, achieving comparable strength and toughness through reduced Co content and additions of W, Nb, and Ti. However, hydrogen environment-assisted cracking (HEAC) is a critical concern for the engineering application of this steel. This study investigated the effect of austenitizing time on the microstructure and HEAC behavior of M54 steel. Microstructure analyses through optical microscopy, X-ray diffraction, electron backscatter diffraction, and transmission electron microscopy revealed that extending austenitizing time beyond 75 min led to noticeable grain growth, dissolution of MC carbides and a reduction of the austenite volume fraction. The prior austenite grain boundaries acted as the preferential pathway for hydrogen atoms to diffuse in M54 steel. The hydrogen diffusion coefficient, crack growth rate and HEAC susceptibility exhibited a peak value after austenitizing treatment for 75 min, which may be due to the combined effect of the austenite fraction and prior austenite grain size. This work elucidates how a specific austenitizing treatment can reduce HEAC risks and proposes an optimized austenitizing protocol for M54 steel.

title: Subsample averaging for non-periodic microstructures: Bias reduction, dispersion increase, and practical trade-offs in computational micromechanics
venue: European Journal of Mechanics A Solids
abstract: The computation of effective properties of random microstructured materials via representative volume elements (RVE) is affected by both bias and dispersion. For non-periodic microstructures (snapshots), which naturally arise in experiments and imaging-based studies, the bias decays slowly, rendering standard homogenization approaches inaccurate, significantly biased, and therefore unreliable. Recent theoretical results suggest that subsample averaging – evaluating the apparent properties only on a strictly interior subdomain – can significantly reduce the bias. In this work, we investigate the practical performance of subsample averaging for linear elastic particle-reinforced composites using large-scale numerical experiments and FFT-based computational micromechanics. We first demonstrate that subsample averaging must respect the Hill–Mandel condition to improve the convergence behavior of the bias, i.e., both stress and strain fields must be subsample averaged. In particular, the naive approach of subsample averaging the apparent stress alone may reduce the magnitude of the bias, but does not improve its convergence rate. When applied consistently, subsample averaging reduces the magnitude of the bias and produces a more favorable decay trend for the investigated non-periodic microstructures. However, this bias reduction comes at the cost of an increased dispersion due to the reduced sampling domain, resulting in only marginal improvements of the total error when used in isolation. To overcome this limitation, we combine subsample averaging with variance reduction via optimized volume fraction (OVF), which significantly improves overall accuracy and reliability for matrix-inclusion composites. The presented strategy is straightforward to implement and can be readily applied within existing computational frameworks without modifying the underlying solver. These results reveal a fundamental bias–dispersion trade-off associated with subsample averaging and provide practical guidance for computing the effective properties from non-periodic microstructure samples, including samples obtained experimentally.

title: Physical decoupling and kinetic mechanisms of the combustion inertness of pressurized coal gasification fine slag
abstract: Pressurized coal gasification fine slag (PGFS) shows low combustion reactivity due to ash encapsulation. Using gravity separation, high-carbon PGFS-HC was obtained with ash content reduced to 10.73 wt% and SBET increased to 253 m2 & sdot;g-1. Its comprehensive combustion index S increased from 0.09 & times; 10-8 to 14.84 & times; 10-8. TG-MS analysis shows that the CO2 release peak in PGFS-HC coincides with the DTG peak, whereas it is delayed in raw PGFS, indicating that mass transfer limitation rather than carbon graphitization dominates combustion inertness. These results demonstrate that targeted removal of the physical ash barrier is key to improving PGFS combustion and enables cascade utilization of high-carbon and high-ash fractions.

title: Provable tensor robust principal component analysis via adaptive convex-concave regularization
abstract: Balancing computational efficiency with reconstruction accuracy remains a core challenge in high-dimensional tensor recovery. We propose Adaptive Convex-Concave Tensor Robust Principal Component Analysis (AC2-TRPCA), which jointly leverages data-adaptive column-orthogonal subspace learning within a reduced-core representation and a convex-concave singular value separation strategy. A nonconvex regularizer applied to the reduced core tensor yields a tighter rank approximation and substantially lowers computational and memory complexity. On the theoretical side, we establish an approximate recovery guarantee under a modified tensor incoherence condition and prove that the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM)-based algorithm converges to a generalized Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) point. Experiments on synthetic data, hyperspectral image denoising, and video background modeling demonstrate that AC2-TRPCA improves reconstruction accuracy by 1.9-4.0 dB while substantially reducing runtime overhead, enabling the processing of large-scale tensors within a fraction of the time required by existing approaches. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/chy0926/Provable-Tensor-Robust-Principal-Component-Analysis-via-Adaptive-Convex-C oncave-Regularization.

title: Tailored graphene quantum dots improve heavy-metal immobilization in municipal solid waste incineration fly ash under low-cement conditions
abstract: Cement solidification/stabilization is widely used to immobilize heavy metals in municipal solid waste incineration fly ash (IFA), but the need for relatively high cement dosages increases the volume of solidified products, treatment cost, and landfill pressure. This study hypothesizes that highly dispersed, oxygen-functionalized graphene quantum dots (GQDs) can enhance heavy metal immobilization under low-cement conditions by promoting hydration-product formation and providing additional metal-binding sites. To test this hypothesis, tailored GQDs were synthesized and incorporated into cement-IFA matrices with a cement-to-IFA mass ratio of 1:5. The immobilization performance and mechanism were evaluated using combined leaching, speciation, microstructural, solution removal, and molecular dynamics analyses. The optimized GQD-modified matrix reduced Pb, Cd, and Zn leaching by 61.7-85.6% and promoted their transformation into more stable chemical fractions. Multiscale analyses indicate that GQDs promote the formation and polymerization of calcium (alumino) silicate hydrate gels, thereby strengthening the physical encapsulation of heavy metals. Meanwhile, oxygen-containing surface groups on GQDs interact with heavy metal ions and suppress their mobility. These synergistic effects improve heavy metal immobilization in the low-cement IFA treatment system. This study provides a feasible strategy for enhancing hazardous IFA treatment under low-cement conditions and suggests a potential engineering application for GQDs.

title: Enzyme-responsive Pickering emulsion-incorporated whey protein coating-forming system: Preparation, properties and application in banana preservation
abstract: We developed a pectin methylesterase (PME)-responsive whey protein coating for postharvest preservation of bananas. The coating incorporated a whey protein isolate-low methoxyl pectin (WPI-LMP) nanocomplexstabilized Pickering emulsion containing a mixed oil phase of thyme essential oil and soybean oil (TEOPE). At an oil-phase fraction of 40%, TEOPE exhibited an average particle size of 693 nm and a zeta-potential of-59 mV, while maintaining a high loading of active compounds and preventing droplet aggregation. The WPI film containing 1.5% (v/v) TEOPE exhibited an elongation at break of 83.21%, accompanied by significantly enhanced overall barrier properties. Moreover, PME-triggered de-esterification of LMP progressively disrupted the WPI-LMP nanocomplex as the PME concentration increased from 0 to 4 mg/mL, leading to an increase in the cumulative release of thyme essential oil (TEO) from 16% to 42%. In preservation trials, the WPI coating containing TEOPE effectively delayed fruit browning, reduced weight loss rate to 5.93%, and maintained hardness, with only a 35.59% reduction compared to 57.19% in the control group. Furthermore, owing to its enzyme-triggered release mechanism, the coating provided sustained antimicrobial protection. Compared with the WPI-TEO treatment, the WPI-TEOE1.5 coating more effectively suppressed microbial proliferation during the later stages of storage, resulting in a lower total viable count at day 10 (4.70 vs. 5.08 log CFU/g). These results indicate that the coating represents a promising and sustainable strategy for extending the shelf life of perishable fruits.

title: Nanoconfinement and wettability alteration govern crude-oil persistence in high-porosity mudstone with nm-sized pores
abstract: High-porosity mudstone with nm-sized pores is a potentially low-cost and widely available mineral sorbent for crude-oil spill remediation, but its practical reuse depends on whether oil-induced pore blockage and wettability alteration can be effectively reversed after cleaning. Here, three mudstones were investigated in raw, crude-oilimmersed, and solvent-extracted states using X-ray microscopy, N2 physisorption, dynamic vapor sorption, contact-angle measurements, FTIR (Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy) and XPS (X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy), and contrast-variation small-angle neutron scattering. Crude-oil immersion markedly reduced accessible pore volume and surface area, suppressed the low-pressure adsorption responses of water, octane, and toluene, and shifted all three mudstones from strongly water-wet to hydrophobic behavior. Water contact angles increased from 8.5 to 26.4 degrees in the raw state to 94.0-121.1 degrees after oil immersion, and remained at 72.9-78.8 degrees after solvent extraction. Across the three samples, BET (Brunauer, Emmett, and Teller) surface area decreased from 12.6-88.8 to 1.30-29.3 m2/g after oil immersion and recovered to 12.0-86.0 m2/g after extraction, indicating substantial reopening of the pore network but incomplete restoration of interfacial properties. FTIR and XPS analyses further indicate that persistent organic residues, especially resin/asphaltene-rich fractions, remained on mineral surfaces after extraction. Accordingly, solvent-cleaned mudstone should be regarded as a partially regenerated sorbent rather than a fully restored pristine material, with important implications for sorbent reuse and post-remediation management.

title: A simulation study of X-ray-induced acoustic dosimetry for a compact FLASH radiotherapy device using digital phantoms
abstract: FLASH radiotherapy (FLASH-RT) is a novel technique characterized by its capacity to deliver ultra-high radiation doses to tumor sites within fractions of a second, thereby effectively sparing normal tissues while maintaining therapeutic efficacy against tumors. The X-ray-based FLASH-RT holds particular promise for clinical adoption due to its accessibility to ultra-high-dose-rate beams, compact accelerator design, and reduced treatment costs. Accurate dosimetric verification during FLASH-RT delivery necessitates online monitoring and visualization of spatial dose distribution within the irradiation target. However, the extreme radiotherapy conditions pose substantial challenges to conventional dosimetry methods, such as signal saturation and measurement inaccuracies caused by pair production effects. To address these challenges, in this study, we propose and evaluate an X-ray-induced acoustic imaging (XAI) approach for in-phantom dosimetry in FLASH-RT. Using the Monte Carlo (MC) simulation toolkit Geant4, we modeled the irradiation of three heterogeneous tissue-mimicking phantoms with a single-pulse X-ray beam delivered by a 10 MV medical linear accelerator (Linac) integrated into a compact FLASH radiotherapy device. The generation, propagation, and attenuation of the induced acoustic waves following irradiation from the Linac were approximated using the k-space pseudospectral method. The acoustic signals were collected by a 128-element annular array transducer and subsequently used to reconstruct the spatial dose distribution within the phantoms. The results demonstrate the feasibility of XAI-based dosimetry for ultra-high-dose-rate X-ray beams even under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions, providing a preliminary basis for its further development toward clinical FLASH-RT applications.

title: CFD-PBM modeling and optimization of multiphase flow and crystallization in an industrial wet-process phosphoric acid reactor
abstract: Industrial wet-process phosphoric acid (WPA) reactors operated by the dihydrate process involve strongly coupled multiphase flow, reactive mass transfer, and calcium sulfate dihydrate crystallization, together with pronounced spatial non-uniformity. To resolve these coupled phenomena, a CFD-PBM model was developed on the platform of OpenFOAM. Gas-liquid-solid three-phase flow was described using the Eulerian multi-fluid method, with coupled heat transfer, species transport, reaction kinetics, and crystal nucleation, growth, agglomeration, and breakage. The rotation of the impellers was represented by the multiple reference frame (MRF) method. A 400 kt/a industrial WPA unit with six reaction tanks in series was considered, and Tank 3 was selected as a representative domain because severe scaling and deposition occurred in the middle tanks, while single-tank modeling reduced computational cost. The model was validated against crystal size distribution data, and was then used to analyze operating parameters and optimize the locations of the passages between adjacent tanks. The simulated crystal size distribution agreed well with experimental data reported in the literature, with a mean relative deviation of about 14.7 %. The effects of operating parameters were then explored. Higher temperature increased the consumption of phosphate rock and sulfuric acid, while enhancing gas yield. Increased impeller speed improved mixing, diminished stagnant zones and refined crystal sizes. Moving the passage toward the side wall improved the main circulation path, decreasing the stagnant-zone fraction from 9.4 % to 6.6 % and increasing H3PO4 production. The results provide a theoretical method for structural optimization and crystallization-process intensification in industrial WPA reactors.

title: Benchmarking reference-based cellular deconvolution algorithms to predict cell proportions
abstract: Computational cellular deconvolution enables researchers to estimate the proportions of distinct cell types in bulk RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) samples using single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) as a reference. This offers a scalable and cost-effective alternative to physical cell separation. Despite recent advancements in cellular deconvolution methods, rigorous comparative benchmarking across diverse conditions and independent datasets remains limited. Here we present a systematic benchmarking study of ten reference-based deconvolution algorithms: MuSiC, DWLS, BayesPrism, CIBERSORTx, SCDC, BisqueRNA, DISSECT, TAPE, Scaden, and scpDeconv. The algorithms were selected based on architectural diversity and popularity in the field. We evaluate these methods through six experiments using two independent datasets. Under baseline conditions, MuSiC, DWLS, and BayesPrism achieved the strongest performance (mean per-sample Pearson correlation coefficient r>0.95; Lin's concordance correlation coefficient CCC >0.95), while deep learning methods showed greater variability. Depth robustness experiments revealed that SCDC and DWLS were most stable across four sequencing-depth levels. Reference mismatch analysis showed that restricting the scRNA-seq reference to a single developmental stage substantially reduced average performance, with mean Pearson r across stage-restricted references ranging from 0.17 to 0.58 across methods; BayesPrism showed the highest average robustness. Overall, these results provide practical guidance for selecting deconvolution methods under different conditions. The code used to run the experiments on each algorithm is publicly available on GitHub at https://github.com/compbiolabucf/Benchmarking-Deconvolution-Algorithms.

title: Enhancing CO2 sequestration in saline aquifers using AOT-modified silica aerogel nanoparticles: synthesis, stability, and pore-scale flow dynamics
abstract: This study presents the synthesis, characterization, and performance evaluation of AOT-SA nanoparticles for enhanced CO 2 sequestration in saline aquifers. Hydrophobic silica aerogel nanoparticles were synthesized via a sol–gel process and subsequently modified with the anionic surfactant sodium dioctyl sulfosuccinate (AOT) to impart brine compatibility. Comprehensive characterization (BET, FESEM-EDS, FTIR, Raman) confirmed a mesoporous structure (79.5 m 2 /g surface area) with successful AOT surface adsorption. Colloidal stability tests in brines of varying ionic composition (0–45,000 ppm NaCl, 0–700 ppm MgCl 2 ) showed the modified nanoparticles maintained a high negative zeta potential, indicating stable dispersion. Wettability alteration experiments on oil-aged sandstone and carbonate rocks identified an optimal nanofluid concentration of 80 ppm, which significantly reduced the CO 2 -brine-rock contact angle. Crucially, pore-scale flow visualization in two-dimensional heterogeneous micromodels revealed that this optimal nanofluid reduced viscous fingering, delayed CO 2 breakthrough, and increased the fraction of pore volume accessed by CO 2 by up to 92% compared to nanoparticle-free brine. The work demonstrates that AOT-SA nanoparticles function as a multifunctional agent that concurrently addresses colloidal stability in saline environments, desirable wettability alteration, and improved pore-scale displacement efficiency, offering a tangible strategy to increase CO 2 storage security in saline formations.

title: Deep oxidative desulfurization in a continuous-flow fixed-bed system over acid-regulated tungsten-oxide/resin catalyst
abstract: Deep desulfurization of model fuel oils is important for reducing SOx emissions and meeting increasingly stringent fuel-sulfur regulations. However, the translation of oxidative desulfurization (ODS) from batch operation to a cost-effective and reusable continuous-flow system remains challenging. Herein, a tungsten-oxide immobilized macroporous D301 resin catalyst (WxOy/D301) was prepared by a facile ion-exchange-assisted immobilization strategy, in which protonated tertiary amine sites in D301 anchor tungstate-derived W(VI) oxide species while retaining liquid-phase accessibility. Using H2O2 as a green oxidant and H3PO4 as an acid regulator, the batch system achieved > 99% dibenzothiophene (DBT) conversion at 70 degrees C and an O/S molar ratio of 4.15. When transferred to a fixed-bed reactor (70 degrees C, O/S = 8.3, residence time = 30 min), the separated oil phase from a 2500 ppm S DBT model oil was reduced to below 10 ppm sulfur, and stable desulfurization was maintained after the initial bed-stabilization period. The practical advantage of this approach lies in combining a low-cost commercial resin support, high tungsten loading, catalyst retention in a packed bed, and spontaneous oil/polar-phase separation after reaction, which reduces post-reaction catalyst separation and supports process intensification. Raman spectroscopy indicates the formation of H2O2-derived peroxo-tungsten species, while EPR spin trapping provides complementary evidence for transient -OOH-related oxygen-centered species and no dominant hydroxyl-radical pathway. Thus, DBT oxidation is mainly attributed to a peroxo-tungsten-mediated electrophilic oxygen-transfer pathway promoted by the acidic microenvironment. These results provide a promising model-oil demonstration for developing acid-regulated tungsten-oxide/resin fixed-bed systems, while further validation with real fuel fractions and long-term leaching analysis remains necessary for industrial application.

title: Surfactant-assisted Nd incorporation regulates lattice distortion and oxygen defects in electrodeposited Ti/PbO2 coatings for enhanced electrocatalytic oxidation
abstract: Rational control of the surface structure and defect chemistry of PbO2 electrodes is essential for electrocatalytic oxidation, yet the role of surfactant-mediated rare-earth incorporation in regulating lattice structure and interfacial reactivity remains unclear. Here, STAB-assisted electrodeposition was used to construct Nd-doped Ti/PbO2 electrodes by regulating crystal growth, Nd incorporation, and surface oxygen chemistry. STAB addition produced dense, refined coatings and increased Nd enrichment. The optimized TA2 electrode exhibited the largest relative (3-PbO2 (101) low-angle displacement, the maximum microstrain (0.497%, 23.9% above TA0), the highest (3-PbO2 fraction, the highest XPS Nd content (0.15 at.%), and an Oads/Olat ratio of 0.90. These structural changes coincided with an oxygen evolution potential of 2.66 V vs. SHE and a charge-transfer resistance of 14.01 Omega cm2, indicating delayed oxygen evolution and accelerated interfacial charge transfer. Chlorine evolution kinetics improved without changing the Volmer-Tafel pathway, while hydroxyl-radical generation and operational stability were enhanced, accompanied by reduced Pb release. In actual desulfurization wastewater, TA2 achieved chloride and COD removal efficiencies of 90.4% and 74.4%, respectively. These results establish a relationship among STAB-dependent Nd enrichment, lattice distortion, surface oxygen chemistry, and electrocatalytic activity, providing a practical strategy for engineering functional PbO2 coatings.

title: Development of a phenomenological spray model for next generation dual-fuel marine engines: validation in free-field conditions
abstract: This study develops and validates a reduced-order phenomenological spray model for dual-fuel marine engines operating under reactivity controlled compression ignition (RCCI) conditions. Rather than introducing a new spray-theory class, the work adapts a Musculus-based formulation into an RCCI-oriented framework capable of predicting both spray penetration and cylinder-fixed fuel–air stratification at low computational cost. The main methodological advance is the introduction of a CV-to-zone mapping strategy for transferring spray control-volume information into the zonal structure required by multi-zone combustion models; among the three tested approaches, an angled non-uniform mapping gave the most accurate stratification representation. Validation is via high-speed optical measurements by the Optical Spray Combustion Chamber and high-fidelity CFD simulations with CONVERGE. Sensitivity analysis identified the discharge coefficient (Ca) and velocity profile factor (β) as dominant calibration parameters, with profile evolution factor (α) serving as a secondary shaper of radial distribution. A two-stage optimization strategy for local tuning per case and global tuning across conditions demonstrated that the globally calibrated model reproduces spray penetration within ∼14% of CFD, and peak high-reactivity fuel location within ±2 zones across calibration and validation datasets. Amplitude prediction of peak fuel fraction exhibited larger scatter (∼40%), but location fidelity was robust. The framework provides a reliable and computationally efficient surrogate for spray-mixing dynamics and is well suited for future integration with fast 0D/1D multi-zone combustion models to support predictive, cycle-resolved simulation of advanced RCCI engines.

title: Feedstock-specific effects of sulfur-rich vegetable fractions on food waste anaerobic digestion: Sulfide-associated redox perturbation and adaptive microbial reassembly
abstract: Food waste (FW) anaerobic digestion (AD) is strongly affected by feedstock heterogeneity, yet the role of sulfur-rich vegetable fractions remains poorly defined. Here, garlic (GAR), Chinese cabbage (CHC), and cabbage (CAB) were used as representative sulfur-rich vegetables to assess their effects on methane production, redox status, and microbial function during FW AD. At equal volatile solids loading, GAR showed no significant effect, whereas CHC and CAB caused a biphasic response, with delayed methane accumulation and reduced cumulative yield followed by late-stage daily methane production 39.6% and 45.9% higher than the control, respectively. CHC and CAB promoted sulfide accumulation and elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS) during the early stage. Elevated ROS levels were associated with lower NADH/NAD+ ratios, reduced electron transport activity, and volatile fatty acid accumulation, collectively indicating a redox-perturbed state characterized by functional decoupling between acidogenesis and methanogenesis. Metagenomic analysis showed that this early disturbance was followed by functional reassembly of the community. Hydrolytic-acidogenic bacteria sustained fermentation, accompanied by enrichment of genes associated with PFOR-Rnf-mediated energy conservation and the ED and oxidative PPP pathways, while methanogenesis shifted toward acetoclastic and methylotrophic routes. Genome-resolved analysis attributed the genomic potential for PFOR-Rnf-mediated energy conservation to Aminobacterium and Defluviitoga MAGs, and showed that Methanosarcina possessed the broadest oxidative stress defense repertoire, supporting its dominance after ROS perturbation. These findings provide a mechanistic framework linking sulfur-rich feedstock heterogeneity to methane-production dynamics, involving sulfide-associated redox perturbation and subsequent microbial functional reassembly.

title: CFD-based applicability assessment and multi-objective optimization of nanocomposite coating deposition by air-assisted atomization spraying: Thickness uniformity, effective coverage area, Gaussian-fitting NRMSE, and coefficient of variation
abstract: Background: Air-assisted atomization spraying (AAAS) has attracted considerable attention as a cost-effective and efficient technique for fabricating nanocomposite coatings. However, previous studies have mainly focused on small-scale spraying of nanoparticle systems, whereas large-area spray deposition has rarely been investigated. Methods: In this study, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) was employed to numerically investigate the deposition behavior of different nanoparticles on a large flat substrate. The effects of nanoparticle type, volume fraction, nozzle feed rate, and air pressure on the deposition profile, effective coverage area, Gaussian-fitting NRMSE, and coefficient of variation (CV) were systematically analyzed. To balance coating uniformity and coverage area, response surface methodology (RSM) combined with the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) was adopted for multi-objective optimization. Significant findings: The results indicate that all five nanoparticle systems are capable of forming stable coatings, thereby demonstrating the applicability of AAAS to nanocomposite coating fabrication. Compared with the coating at a nanoparticle volume fraction of 1%, the coating at 5% exhibits a thickness distribution closer to the ideal Gaussian profile, although its effective coverage area is reduced by 26.8%. In addition, increasing the feed rate and air pressure reduced the uniformity of the coating thickness distribution, while significantly enlarging the effective coverage area. Under the optimized conditions, the Gaussian-fitting NRMSE and effective coverage area reached 8.51% and 3.39 & times; 104 mm2, respectively, corresponding to a nanoparticle volume fraction of 2.94%, a feed rate of 4.88 g/s, and an air pressure of 0.128 MPa.

title: Enhancing network robustness under regional failures via cut module-driven resource-optimal link safeguarding
abstract: Complex networks are widely used in critical infrastructures such as communications, transportation, and power systems, yet regional failures can disrupt network functionality and severely threaten system reliability. Existing approaches to robustness enhancement often face high computational complexity or limited applicability. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a scalable link safeguard algorithm designed for large-scale networks. Node cut values are computed via pruned trees to identify vulnerable links. Building on this, cut modules are further selected based on node degrees, enabling more precise localization of network bottlenecks. After removing these cut modules, links in the resulting minimum-cost spanning tree are prioritized for safeguarding, thereby efficiently enhancing network connectivity. The proposed algorithm achieves the target connectivity for all nodes in the graph at a low solution cost across various small-scale networks. Competing methods either demand a five-orders-of-magnitude higher runtime to achieve the same proportion of qualified nodes or incur a higher cost while only enabling a smaller fraction of nodes to meet the target connectivity. Experiments on real-world Internet Service Provider (ISP) topologies further show that the algorithm rapidly produces low-cost solutions with near-optimal performance. For large-scale graphs, the algorithm ensures that nearly all nodes reach the target connectivity after multiple iterations, and the average runtime is approximately 230 seconds. With parallelization, the runtime can be further reduced to a few seconds, while the protection cost accounts for only 20% of the total link weight. Further comparative experiments with state-of-the-art methods show that the proposed algorithm consistently achieves superior performance at a lower safeguarding cost. These results collectively demonstrate that the proposed algorithm is effective and provide a new perspective on robustness enhancement in complex networks.

title: Energy, Environmental, and Economic Impacts of Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF) and Biomass-Derived Fuel (BDF) Mixes with Consideration of Fuel Mixing Ratios
Do We Really Need Diffusion? A Fast U-Net for Paired Medical Image Translation
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging-signal fat fraction (MRI-SFF) quantifies tissue fat and serves as an established biomarker for metabolic and musculoskeletal disorders. The acquisition requires, however, specialized MRI sequences, which are not available routinely. We investigate whether SFF can be estimated from widely available T2-weighted (T2w) MRI via image-to-image translation (I2I). We further compare a lightweight 4-level U-Net to a state-of-the-art Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) using a dataset of 230 048 paired 2D images (183 517 train, 23 621 val, 22 910 test) from the German National Cohort (NAKO). Both models clearly outperform the identity baseline (Pearson correlation r = 0.769, mean absolute error MAE = 0.070 +/- 0.054), which confirms that the models learn a non-trivial cross-modal mapping. Interestingly, the lightweight U-Net outperforms the DDPM in both correlation (r = 0.975 vs. 0.962) and error (MAE = 0.014 +/- 0.015 vs. 0.019 +/- 0.019), while reducing inference time by a factor of 208 (25.2 ms vs. 5 227.2 ms per image using 50 Denoising Diffusion Implicit Model (DDIM) steps). The strong clinical performance at substantially reduced computational cost enables real-time clinical use.

title: Engineering synergies between thermochemical and biochemical processes for municipal solid waste management and sustainable fuels supply
abstract: Municipal solid waste (MSW) valorization is constrained by the mismatch between heterogeneous feedstock properties and the operating requirements of individual conversion technologies. This review synthesizes integrated thermochemical and biochemical pathways and treats MSW valorization as a system design problem organized around carbon cascading, in which each carbon fraction is routed to the process able to convert it and performance is governed by interactions between processes rather than by individual process yields. Four hybrid routes are examined: gasification-syngas fermentation, pyrolysis-anaerobic digestion, hydrothermal processing-anaerobic digestion, and reverse configurations in which digestion precedes thermochemical conversion. Across these routes, intermediate quality rather than process yield governs feasibility. Tar (1-150 g/Nm3), ammonia (up to 14,000 ppmv), and sulfur species must be reduced by two to three orders of magnitude before downstream bioconversion, relocating the critical engineering problem from the reactor to the interface. Environmental and economic evidence indicates that integration benefits are real but conditional. Coupling anaerobic digestion with pyrolysis approximately doubled the climate mitigation of standalone digestion, yet the advantage is not uniform across impact categories, and one configuration achieved the greatest climate benefit while increasing freshwater ecotoxicity 52-fold. Reported production costs for integrated routes ($0.31-1.95/L ethanol) exceed those of standalone biochemical conversion, though integrated systems convert carbon that cheaper routes cannot access, and scale and product value influence viability more than process configuration. Integration is therefore justified by feedstock coverage and interface management rather than by coupling processes as such, and full-chain demonstration on real MSW remains the principal research challenge.

title: Dynamic modeling of proton exchange membrane and alkaline water electrolyzers under fluctuating renewable energy: A comparative review and unified framework
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy is shifting water electrolysis for hydrogen production from steady-state operation to dynamic conditions involving frequent load changes, low-load operation, overload, and repeated start-stop cycles. Proton exchange membrane (PEM) and alkaline (ALK) water electrolyzers are the two most widely deployed low-temperature electrolysis technologies, but they differ substantially in ion-conducting media, reactant transport pathways, gas evolution behavior, thermal management, and intrinsic time constants. These differences lead to distinct transient responses, performance evolution, and degradation risks under fluctuating power inputs. This review provides a critical and comparative synthesis of dynamic modeling studies on PEM and ALK electrolyzers under renewable-energy-driven operation. Existing models are examined from three interrelated perspectives: spatial non-uniformity of state variables, dynamic evolution and degradation of key performance parameters, and bidirectional multiphysics coupling with feedback closure. The analysis shows that PEM models should retain local current density, membrane water content, temperature gradients, membrane conductivity, and interfacial impedance, whereas ALK models should emphasize KOH concentration, electrolyte circulation, bubble coverage, gas void fraction, effective reaction area, and separator resistance. Highfidelity models provide mechanistic insight into local transport, thermal, and electrochemical processes, but their system-level application is limited by extensive parameter requirements and high computational cost. Reducedorder models are more suitable for control and operational optimization, yet may omit critical feedback pathways. Future research should prioritize dominant-state retention, dynamic parameter updating, feedback-loop closure, engineering deployability, and standardized validation under fluctuating operating conditions.

title: Enhanced thermal management of pouch lithium-ion cells via phase change material, foam and wavy fin integrated hybrid air cooling
